feat.name: Cleaving Adept
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Full Coverage
entries: When you make the second attack of the Cleave mastery, the second target can be any creature within your reach, not just one within 5 feet of the first target.

entries.name: Sweeping Slash
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can substitute an attack to make a sweeping slash. Make a single melee attack roll with a weapon which you can use the Cleave mastery of and compare the result to the AC of each enemy creature within your reach. If the result meets or exceeds the creature's AC, it takes the weapon's damage, but you don't add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can use this ability only once per turn.

feat.name: Friends in Low Places
entries: You gain three close contacts which you can call upon to aid you on your adventures. You determine their appearance, and they use the Contact stat block below.

Over the course of an hour, which can take place during a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can summon one of these contacts to your side. Your contact acts independently of you, but it obeys your commands.

entries.name: Combat
entries: The contact is an ally to you and your allies. It shares your initiative, but takes it's turn immediately after yours.

Disappearance of your Contact. A contact dies if it drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, or is dismissed when you die. You can replace a dead contact over the course of 24 hours and by spending 100 GP.

entries.name: One Contact Only
entries: You can't have more than one contact active at a time. If you summon another contact while one is active, the previous one is dismissed.

feat.name: Noble Bearing
entries: You are a member of the upper class, and it shows. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Mark of Nobility
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} of Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) and Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) checks when interacting with members of the upper class.

entries.name: Noble Presence
entries: You can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to snap an ally back into focus. Choose one ally that can hear you within 120 feet of you that is {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB}. That condition ends on the ally and they gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to two times your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.
Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Protector
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Interception
entries: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you would be hit by an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to intercept the attack. You move to the nearest unoccupied space within 5 feet of that creature and swap places, and you are hit by the attack instead. This movement doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}, but if your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is 0 or you are otherwise unable to reach the creature to swap places (e.g. they are in the air and you can't fly), this ability has no effect.

If you are dropped to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} after using this feature, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB|Death Saving Throws} until you are {@variantrule Stable|XPHB}, or die.

entries.name: Righteous Protector
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) checks to convince people to let you help them.

feat.name: Acid Glands
entries: Through some means you have developed glands that allow you to spit acid, gaining the following benefits.

entries.name: Acid Resistance
entries: You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Acid damage.

entries.name: Spit
entries: You have grown acid glands which count as a simple ranged weapon you are proficient with. Your acid spit has a short range of 30 feet, a long range of 90 feet and the Finesse property. On a hit, they deal 1d8 Acid damage.

feat.name: Amphibious
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Amphibious
entries: You can breathe both air and water.

entries.name: Swim Speed
entries: You gain a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

feat.name: Artist's Creative Conjuring
entries: A connection with The Artist enhances your tricky mind to find clever new spins on old techniques. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Two Cantrips
entries: You learn two cantrips of your choice from any spell list. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat's spells (choose when you select this feat).

entries.name: Fabricate
entries: You learn the {@spell Fabricate|XPHB} spell, and can cast it without expending a spell slot. When you cast it in this way, it has a casting time of an {@variantrule Action|XPHB} and a duration of 10 minutes. After casting it in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast this spell with any spell slots you have of the appropriate level, but with the normal casting time and duration.

feat.name: Blood-Touched
entries: Your exposure to House Varley’s blood magic has changed you, granting you the following benefits:

entries.name: Blood Magic
entries: Choose one level 1 spell from the {@filter Evocation or Transmutation|spells|level=1|school=V;T} school of magic. You always have that spell and the {@spell Enhance Ability|XPHB} spell prepared. You can cast each of these spells without expending a spell slot. Once you cast either spell in this way, you can't cast that spell in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast these spells using spell slots you have of the appropriate level. The spells' spellcasting ability is the ability increased by this feat.

feat.name: Companion Trainer
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Companion Training
entries: Choose one creature you have indefinitely summoned by a class feature, Feat, or the {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} or {@spell Find Steed|XPHB} spells. That creature gains one of the following Feats of your choice: Amphibious, {@feat Athlete|XPHB}, {@feat Charger|XPHB}, {@feat Heavy Armor Master|XPHB}, {@feat Medium Armor Master|XPHB}, {@feat Martial Adept|XPHB}, {@feat Speedy|XPHB}, or Wings Unfurled.
These benefits persist even after the creature is dismissed, resummoned, or changes form.

feat.name: Familiar Trainer
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Familiar Training
entries: Choose one creature you have summoned using the {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell. Its {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} is now equal to yours

In addition, it gains one of the following Feats of your choice: Amphibious, {@feat Athlete|XPHB}, Blood-Touched, {@feat Fey-Touched|XPHB}, {@feat Grappler|XPHB}, {@feat Lucky|XPHB}, {@feat Mage Slayer|XPHB}, {@feat Magic Initiate|XPHB}, {@feat Martial Adept|XPHB}, {@feat Savage Attacker|XPHB}, {@feat Shadow-Touched|XPHB}, {@feat Skilled|XPHB}, {@feat Skulker|XPHB}, {@feat Tavern Brawler|XPHB}, {@feat Telekinetic|XPHB}, {@feat Telepathic|XPHB}, or {@feat Tough|XPHB}. If the Feat doesn't already provide an ability score increase, you can increase one of your familiar's ability scores by 1, to a maximum of 20.
These benefits persist even after the familiar is dismissed, resummoned, or changes form.

feat.name: Lovers' Duality
entries: A connection with the Lovers gifts you a dual nature. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Gemini
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you create a perfect copy of yourself in an unoccupied space you can see within 15 feet of yourself. This feature lasts for 1 minute, but ends early if you dismiss it (no action required) or become {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}. When this feature ends, you decide which version is the real you.

While this copy persists, you are considered to be occupying both spaces at once. Both versions share all game statistics and any effects that are applied to them. It is impossible to discern which is the real you.

You can use this ability a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. While your Gemini is active, the following rules apply:

items.name: Actions
entries: Actions you take that target others can originate from either version of you, you choose when you take that action.

items.name: Movement
entries: When moving, only one version of you moves, but you can divide your movement between your two versions in any way you like.

items.name: Shared Suffering
entries: When only one version of you takes damage from any given source, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to that damage. If both versions are subjected to an area effect, such as from the {@spell Fireball|XPHB} spell, you make one saving throw and take the effects as normal.

feat.name: Paragon's Ward
entries: A connection with The Paragon has gifted you with power to protect your body and convictions. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Paragon's Ward
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you wreath yourself in the energies of the Paragon for 10 minutes. This effect ends early if you dismiss it (no action required) or become {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}. When you activate this feature and as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on subsequent turns, you can grant yourself or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to 3 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. While a creature has these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to end or avoid the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, and against spells from the Illusion or Enchantment schools. Any {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} remaining at the end of the duration are lost.
Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}

feat.name: Poisonous
entries: You have built a tolerance to poison and weaponized it for your own usage, giving you the following benefits.

entries.name: Poison Resistance
entries: You gain resistance to Poison damage and have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Poison Breath
entries: As an action, you can exhale a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} of poisonous gas. All creatures in that area must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 12 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 1d12} Poison damage, or half as much on a successful one.
This damage increases by {@dice 1d12} at levels 5 ({@dice 2d12}), 11 ({@dice 3d12}), and 17 ({@dice 4d12}).

feat.name: Punishing Pushes
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Slam
entries: When a creature affected by your Push mastery collides with a surface or object of Medium size or larger, the creature takes {@damage 1d6} Bludgeoning damage for every 5 feet it traveled.

feat.name: Sapping Strikes
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Exploit Weakness
entries: When an enemy creature affected by your Sap mastery misses with its attack roll, a creature of your choice within reach (including yourself) can make an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB} against the enemy.

feat.name: Primal Mutation
entries: Through a natural or alchemical process you have developed a sharp natural weapon, ensuring you are never unarmed, giving you the following benefits.

entries.name: Natural Weapon
entries: You grow claws (Slashing), fangs (Piercing), horns (Piercing), or hooves (Bludgeoning). When you use your Unarmed Strike and deal damage, you can choose to use this natural weapon. You deal 1d6 damage of the type in parentheses instead of the normal damage of an Unarmed Strike.

feat.name: Savant's Inquiry
entries: A connection with The Savant allows you to know your enemy with each strike you take. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Savant's Inquiry
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you wreath yourself in the energies of the Savant for 1 minute. This effect ends early if you dismiss it (no action required) or become {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}. For the duration, when you hit a creature with an attack roll and deal damage to it, you also deal {@damage 1d8} Psychic damage and pull knowledge about that creature. Choose one of the following statistics from below, and the DM reveals that information about the creature to you:

On a critical hit, the target must make a Wisdom saving throw with a DC equal to 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + the ability score modifier used for the attack roll. On a failure, the DM reveals the entire stat block to you as the Savant's guidance leads to critical, comprehensive information related to your quarry. On a success, you choose two pieces of information from the list above to be revealed by the DM. You can deal this damage and gain this information only once per turn.
You can use this ability a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Shepherd's Embrace
entries: A connection with The Shepherd allows you to lend aid to your allies. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Shepherd's Embrace
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you wreath yourself in the energies of the Shepherd for 1 minute. This effect ends early if you dismiss it (no action required) or become {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}. When you activate this ability and as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on subsequent turns, you can target a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The creature restores {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 2d6} + your Constitution modifier or ends one condition on itself from {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}, {@condition Stunned|XPHB}, {@condition Blinded|XPHB}, or {@condition Deafened|XPHB}.

This ability can only be called forth during combat. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Tool Expert
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Tool Proficiency
entries: You gain proficiency in one tool of your choice.

entries.name: Expertise
entries: Choose one tool which you have proficiency in but lack {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB}. You gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in that tool.

feat.name: Warden's Bond
entries: A connection with The Warden has granted you the pragmatism to make difficult but necessary choices. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Warden's Bond
entries: You always have the {@spell Rary's Telepathic Bond|XPHB} spell prepared. You can cast this spell without expending a spell slot, and when you do, the magic of the Warden deepens the bond. When one of the creatures bonded with the spell takes damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to give the creature {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to that damage, and you receive the same amount of damage.

Once you cast this spell in this way, you can't cast it in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast this spell with any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you select this Feat).

feat.name: Whip Master
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Ability Score Increase
entries: Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

entries.name: Crack
entries: When you hit a target with a whip as part of the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can cause the weapon to deal extra damage to the target. This damage equals your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Whip Mastery
entries: Once per turn when you hit a creature no more than one sizer larger than you with a whip, you can force it to make a Strength or Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + the ability score modifier used to make the attack) or suffer one of the following effects:

items.name: Disarm
entries: The creature drops one item it is holding, which falls harmlessly to the ground in its space.

items.name: Grapple
entries: The creature has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition. While the creature is {@condition grappled} by your whip, you can't use it to make attacks at other targets until the grapple ends.

items.name: Trip
entries: The creature falls {@condition Prone|XPHB}.

feat.name: Wings Unfurled
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Fly Speed
entries: You gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

feat.name: Wolf's Challenge
entries: A connection with the Wolf has gifted you with power to press your foes, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Wolf's Challenge
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can mark one creature you can see within 30 feet of you and immediately move up to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} towards it. This movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks.

While marked, the creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls targeting any creature other than you. Additionally, you ignore {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} and can take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} so long as you are moving towards the marked creature.

This mark lasts for 1 minute, and ends early if you use this ability to mark a different creature, if you end your turn more than 60 feet away from the marked creature, or when you or the marked creature becomes {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

Akin to centaurs, these creatures of the Underdark have the upper body of a humanoid, and the lower body of an arachnid. Their humanoid skin is often starkly pale, intermittent with colouration or patterning matching their arachnid body.

Arachne can be found in small roving families hunting the various beasts that make this dangerous subterranean land their home. An arachne is a rare sight outside of these family units, and even more so on the surface; Their monstrous appearance tends to draw fear or disgust, though they are known to trade with drow enclaves, who see them in a similar light to driders.

When food is scarce, the strongest among their family will leave to forge their own path, allowing the family a better chance at surviving the shortages. These lone arachne may join a different family in their journey or become fully independent.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Spider Climb
entries: You have a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. In addition, at character level 5, you can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

entries.name: Arachne Lineage
entries: The lower half of your body takes one of two forms, Scorpion or Spider. Choose which you belong to when you select this species, and gain its traits:

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 6-8 feet tall)

To the people at large, the Burrowfolk have the most difficulty with life in Altoras. Forced to choose between living in the underground city of New Burrow ruled by the mob or on the Kaiju-infested jungles of Muhana above, they are often drawn to seedy tactics and underhanded methods just to get by. Their cunning, curiosity, and strong survival instincts make them perfect for the job.

Though this is the unfortunate situation for most Burrowfolk, they are no more naturally violent or larcenous than others. But old stereotypes linger, especially with the affluent of New Burrow actively putting their interests above all else.
Burrowfolk are short humanoids that closely resemble members of the rodent family. They mature quickly, often reaching adulthood by age 12, but still live about as long as Humans.

entries.name: Craftiness
entries: You have proficiency in one tool of your choice or one skill of your choice from {@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}, {@skill Medicine|XPHB}, {@skill Nature|XPHB}, {@skill Stealth|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB}.

entries.name: Keen Senses
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Perception|XPHB} skill. You also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks that rely on sound or smell.

entries.name: Scamper
entries: You have a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} and {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Tight Squeeze
entries: You ignore {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} when squeezing through spaces one size smaller than yourself.

entries.name: Burrow Lineage
entries: You are part of a lineage that grants you unique abilities. Choose one of the following lineage options.

items.name: Caster
entries: You know the {@spell Druidcraft|XPHB} cantrip. You also always have the {@spell Jump|XPHB} spell prepared, and can cast it without expending a spell slot. You can cast it in this way once, and regain the ability to do so again when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast this spell with any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for spells granted by this Lineage (choose when you select this Lineage).

items.name: Defender
entries: When you are hit by an attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to enter a defensive stance. Until the start of your next turn, all Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage you take is reduced by a number equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}  (including from the triggering attack). You can use this ability a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Gnasher
entries: Your teeth are simple melee weapons which you are proficient with and can be used to make Unarmed Strikes. They have {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} and deal {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage on a hit. This damage is doubled against objects and structures.

items.name: Squirmer
entries: Opportunity Attacks have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} against you.

items.name: Burrow Lineage (Caster)
entries: You know the {@spell Druidcraft|XPHB} cantrip. You also always have the {@spell Jump|XPHB} spell prepared, and can cast it without expending a spell slot. You can cast it in this way once, and regain the ability to do so again when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast this spell with any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for spells granted by this Lineage (choose when you select this Lineage).

items.name: Burrow Lineage (Defender)
entries: When you are hit by an attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to enter a defensive stance. Until the start of your next turn, all Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage you take is reduced by a number equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}  (including from the triggering attack). You can use this ability a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Burrow Lineage (Gnasher)
entries: Your teeth are simple melee weapons which you are proficient with and can be used to make Unarmed Strikes. They have {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} and deal {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage on a hit. This damage is doubled against objects and structures.

items.name: Burrow Lineage (Squirmer)
entries: Opportunity Attacks have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} against you.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Small (about 2-4 feet tall)

race.name: Gilblin

entries: Once part of the Kamarilik expedition to Jagara, gilblin were once ordinary goblins. When the colony was forced into the sea, the adaptive nature of the goblins allowed them to take on qualities that facilitated their survival. Now they work with the koalinth in their underwater city, trying to carve a home for themselves beneath the waves.

Much like their land-dwelling ancestors, gilblin are short goblinoids with long pointed ears, broad noses, and a penchant for mischief. But their similarities are as numerous as their differences; gilblin skin and hair comes most often in deep blues and greens, but red is also known to appear. They have fins extending from their forearms, complete with webbed hands and feet.

Their most interesting feature is their water jet, an organ found in their hands or throat that propels an intense stream of water. In the sea, it is a purely defensive mechanism, a surprise show of force to unwanted guests. Above water, however, it allows the gilblin to hunt flying prey, disorienting the unsuspecting creature and bringing it closer to where the gilblin can pounce.
As a gilblin, you have these special traits.

entries.name: Amphibious
entries: You can breathe both air and water. You also have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Fey Ancestry
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition

entries.name: Nimble Escape
entries: You can take the Disengage or Hide action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on each of your turns.

entries.name: Water Jet
entries: You have a natural water jet that counts as a simple ranged weapon you are proficient with. It has a short range of 60 feet, a long range of 180 feet, and {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse}. On a hit, the water jet deals {@damage 1d4} Bludgeoning damage plus {@damage 1d4} Cold damage.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Small (about 3-4 feet tall)

The Kor'Rokka of the Koh'Harrun League have resided on the Harra Archipelago for hundreds of years. While the League is a collection of island nations that are populated mostly by Humans, Tritons, and Sea Elves, the Kor'Rokka have integrated into the League and can be found throughout the different cities that dot the islands.

Kor'Rokka have impressive regenerative powers, capable of preventing their bodies from aging. It's because of this that scholars believe the Kor'Rokka are related to trolls, but question whether this ancestry occurs naturally. While they may be physically intimidating, the Kor'Rokka are a generally reserved people, with a culture that values inner peace and careful consideration of one's actions.

Kor'Rokka are reminiscent of trolls in their towering, slender builds and prominent underbite, but that's mostly where the comparison ends. They are an amphibious species complete with webbed fingers and toes, colorful patterning, and sharp quills adorning various parts of their body. When a Kor' Rokka has come of age they choose a name they feel represents them, this name is often a deed, a natural force or entity that they want to embody, or a virtue. This name is private and only given to those closest to them.

entries.name: Amphibious
entries: You can breathe both air and water. You also have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Limited Regeneration
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend one of your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, roll the die, and regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the roll. You can't use this ability if you have taken fire or acid damage since the end of your last turn.

entries.name: Powerful Build
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on any saving throw you make to end the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition. You also count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity.

entries.name: Quills
entries: You have quills adorning your body that count as a simple ranged weapon you are proficient with. They have a short range of 30 feet, a long range of 90 feet, and {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse}. On a hit, the quills deal {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage.

When you hit a creature with your quills and deal damage to it, you can also deal {@damage 2d6} Poison damage to that target. You can deal this damage a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 6-8 feet tall)

The Gnolls of Altoras are hyena-like humanoids known for their savage martial prowess and distinctive cackle. Commonly found in the forests and plains of Cennverai, these people roam the land in clans, the Matriarch being both the most powerful warrior and the wisest leader. These clans are mostly self-sustaining through living off the land or raiding nearby trade caravans.

Their clan activities often lead to them avoiding civilization and being rejected in kind, but beyond the spurn for battle and the menacing laugh are a people capable of the strongest kinship. Those that leave their clans are almost never seen in solitary; Gnolls are powerful and staunch allies, always willing to put their life on the line for their chosen family.

entries.name: A Good Heckling
entries: You know the {@spell Vicious Mockery|XPHB} cantrip. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability (choose when you select this species).

entries.name: Bite
entries: Your sharp teeth are simple melee weapons which you are proficient with and can be used to make Unarmed Strikes. They have {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} and deal {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage on a hit.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls you make with your Bite against {@variantrule Bloodied|XPHB} creatures.

entries.name: Sudden Rush
entries: As an action, you can increase your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} by 60 feet until the end of your current turn.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Rampage
entries: When you reduce an enemy to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can immediately take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to move up to half your speed and make a weapon attack. You can also take this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} if someone else within 15 feet of you reduces an enemy to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.
You can use this trait a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 5-7 feet tall)

The Grung are brightly coloured frog-like humanoids that were originally subjects of the Yuan-ti, at the bottom of the social ladder. They are skilled hunters and assassins, using ambush tactics and their natural poisons to subdue enemies. The tough pads on their fingers and toes allow them to cling to nearly any surface, and stalk the jungle canopies away from danger and on the prowl.

Using their unique skill sets, they were eventually able to rebel against the Yuan-ti and create their own foothold in the jungles of Muhana and Jagara, forming tribes and their own caste system based on skin color.

entries.name: Amphibious
entries:
You can breathe both air and water.
You also have a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Poison Resilience
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage. You also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws you make to end or avoid the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Poisonous Skin
entries: Any creature that grapples you or otherwise comes into direct contact with your skin must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC 10 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or become {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} for 1 minute. A {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} creature no longer in direct contact with you can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the condition on itself on a success.

You can also apply this poison to any weapon as part of an attack with that weapon. On hit, the target takes an additional {@damage 1d12} poison damage and must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 10 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, the target is {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} for 1 minute. They can remake the save at the end of each of their turns, ending the condition on itself on a success. Once you use your poison in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Standing Leap
entries: Your {@variantrule Long Jump|XPHB} is up to 30 feet and your {@variantrule High Jump|XPHB} is up to 15 feet, with or without a running start.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Small (about 2-4 feet tall)

race.name: Harpy

entries: Harpies are the people of legend amongst sailors of the Root Sea League. Sometimes called sirens, they have mostly humanoid bodies, but with scaly legs, clawed feet and hands, and feathers adorning their body akin to scavenging birds, including their large wings. By other humanoid standards, all harpies are female-presenting, which has led some to believe male harpies don't exist. This rumour is unfounded; the reality is that harpies are all intersex, and simply appear "female". The flock acts as one family unit, each member taking turns scavenging and child rearing. Gendered language and roles are virtually nonexistent.

Harpies use their cunning and magical gift of song to lure sailors into harm's way, scavenging on their remains. Every harpy sings a distinct song. While some songs are said to be heartbreaking in their beauty, others are wretched squawking and compel only the magically enthralled.

This cultural practice has garnered a contentious relationship amidst other island nations as well as between harpy flocks. Some flocks have abandoned this tradition, exclusively engaging in scavenging rather than actively leading others to danger, while others still have begun to hunt fish and crustaceans.
As a harpy, you have these special traits.

entries.name: Claws
entries: You have claws that are simple melee weapons which you are proficient with and can be used to make Unarmed Strikes. They have {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} and deal {@damage 2d4} Slashing damage on a hit.

entries.name: Flight
entries: You have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Luring Song
entries: As an action, you begin to sing a luring song. Choose a number of creatures up to or equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} within 60 feet of you that can hear you. Those creatures must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 10 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Constitution modifier) or be {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you until the end of your next turn. While {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, if the target is more than 5 feet from you, the target must move on its turn towards you by the most direct route, trying to get within 5 feet of you. It doesn't avoid {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}; however, before moving into damaging terrain (such as lava or a pit) and whenever it takes damage, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on a success.

On subsequent turns, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to extend the duration of your song to the end of your next turn, up to a maximum of 1 minute. Your song ends early if you choose to end it (no action required), become {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, or die.
After this trait is used, it must be recharged. At the start of your turn, roll {@dice 1d6}. On a roll of 5+, this trait is recharged.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 4-6 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species

race.name: Jackalwere

entries: Residing deep in the deserts of the Planes of Ruin, the jackalwere live in large packs alongside lamia. It is said they were born as servants to a great demon, transformed from ordinary jackals into shape-shifting tricksters. Jackalweres are easily mistaken for werewolves in this respect, but jackalweres aren't supernaturally afflicted -- their jackal forms are their natural state.

Their shapeshifting powers, abyssal heritage, and deceitful nature have garnered them a frightful reputation among the bandits scattered through the Planes -- a reputation that is not entirely unearned, as the jackalwere are known to be fiendishly capable of luring those crossing through their territory into ambushes. For the eldest of the species, it's said the simple act of telling the truth was physically painful, though this trait is not necessarily carried by modern jackalweres.
As a jackalwere, you have these special traits.

entries.name: Bite
entries: Your sharp teeth are simple melee weapons which you are proficient with and can be used to make Unarmed Strikes. They have {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} and deal {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage on a hit. You cannot use this trait if you are in Humanoid Form (see Shape-Shift).

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Shape-Shift
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can shape-shift into a Medium jackal-humanoid hybrid or a Medium humanoid, or you can return to your true jackal form. Your game statistics, other than your size, are the same in each form. You determine the appearance of each form, but they remain consistent each time you shift in and out of them. Your clothing and equipment aren't changed by this trait, but can be merged into your form (your choice), and your ability to handle them is dependent on the form's arrangement of limbs. You revert to your true form when you die. Each form has specific benefits, seen below:

items.name: Jackal Form
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against a creature if at least one of your allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

items.name: Hybrid Form
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) and Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) checks.

items.name: Humanoid Form
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) checks.

entries.name: Sleep Gaze
entries: As an action, you can force one creature you can see and that can see you within 30 feet to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 10 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). Constructs and Undead succeed automatically. On a failed save, The target has the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition for 10 minutes or until it takes damage or a creature within 5 feet of it takes an action to wake it. On a success, the target is immune to your Sleep Gaze for 24 hours.
After this trait is used, it must be recharged. At the start of your turn, roll {@dice 1d6}. On a roll of 5+, this trait is recharged.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Small (about 2-3 feet tall)

entries.name: Ancestral Legacy
entries: If you replace a species with this lineage, you can keep any Climb, Fly, or Swim Speeds you gained from it.
If you don't keep any of those elements or you choose this lineage at character creation, you gain proficiency in {@skill Nature|XPHB} and {@skill Animal Handling|XPHB}.

entries.name: Phytosis
entries: You have been changed by nature magic, a fact represented by the following benefits:

items: You have an ageless body after reaching maturity. You stop aging physically and cannot die of old age unless aged by magic.
You do not need to eat, though you can still sustain yourself off of food if you so choose.
You don't need to sleep, and magic can't put you to sleep. You can finish a long rest in 4 hours if you spend those hours in an inactive, motionless state, during which you retain consciousness.

entries.name: Phytokinesis
entries: You know the {@spell Thorn Whip|XPHB} cantrip. When you reach character level 3, you learn the {@spell Entangle|XPHB} spell and at character level 5, you learn the {@spell Spike Growth|XPHB} spell. You always have these spells prepared. You can cast them once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast them in that way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast these spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast with this trait (choose the ability when you select this species).

entries.name: Sun's Bounty
entries: As a Magic action, you can grant yourself a shield of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to two times your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. When a hostile creature within 10 feet of you reduces those {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} to 0, it becomes under the effects of the {@spell Faerie Fire|XPHB} spell until the end of your next turn.
You can use this trait a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and regain all expended uses after finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 4-6 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall), chosen when you gain this lineage

The Requiem are a displaced group of divine humanoids, survivors from a universe before this one that was completely unmade. The Requiem are innately tied to the Song of Creation, so while all felt the despair of the end of the Universe from facing their mortality, The Requiem also felt it innately, deeply connected to the very thing being unraveled. When their world was destroyed a small population fled aboard the Mythallar, a magic stasis pod that could sustain them outside of the Universe for millennia. Now, having woken from the Mythallar in a brand new world that's reminiscent of their lost one, they are trying to make Altoras a new home for the future generations born here connected to this reality.

Created by a long-dead god that preceded The Seven in the image of his lost daughter, most Requiem are born female-presenting with tall and slender features reminiscent of Elves. They mature at the same rate as Humans, but live slightly longer - up to 150 years - thanks to the divine resilience granted by their creator.

entries.name: Discordant Melody
entries: When you hit a target with an attack and deal damage to it, you can also deal {@damage 1d8} Thunder damage to that target. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Elating Melody
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, a creature of your choice within 60 feet of you gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 1d8} + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. You can use this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Forged from Divinity
entries: Your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum increases by 1, and it increases by 1 again whenever you gain a level.

entries.name: Keen Senses
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Perception|XPHB} skill. You also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks that rely on sound.

entries.name: Sound Hardened
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Thunder damage.

entries.name: Religious Performer
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) checks that rely on singing, and when you {@action Utilize|XPHB} a {@item Musical Instrument|XPHB}.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 5-7 feet tall)

Originating in the Feywild - a realm of pure emotion - satyrs thrive on the energy of merriment. They resemble elves but have goatlike legs, cloven hooves, and ram or goat horns. The magic of the fey realm has given them an innate ability to perform, to delight, and to resist magical intrusion. While they're usually found in the Feywild, satyrs do wander to other planes of existence, most often to the Material Plane. There they seek to bring a bit of their home plane's splendor to other worlds.

entries.name: Bounding Leaps
entries: Your {@variantrule Long Jump|XPHB} distance is doubled, and you don't provoke Opportunity Attacks when jumping out of reach of a creature.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Fey Ancestry
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Fey Guile
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Performance|XPHB} or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB} skill.

entries.name: Ram
entries: You have horns that count as a simple melee weapon you are proficient with and can be used to make Unarmed Strikes. Your horns have {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse}, and deal {@damage 1d6} Bludgeoning damage on a hit.

entries.name: Seasonal Shift
entries: Each court has extra magic they bring to the Satyr as well as cosmetic changes. The physical changes can be dramatic or subtle and are tied to the season the court represents. Your chosen season grants you special abilities, as seen below. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can shift between the court you draw your power from.

items.name: Autumn Augury
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can call on the changing seasons to guide your senses. Until the end of your next turn, you can see {@condition Invisible|XPHB} creatures and objects and creatures in the Ethereal Plane. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Spring Palms
entries: Your words and songs carry healing magic with them. As an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, you can make a Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB} or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check. One creature of your choice within 60 feet of you that can see or hear you regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the check total. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Summersault
entries: The summer breeze flows through your every move. When you fall, you reduce the damage you take by an amount equal to five times your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

items.name: Winter Wallop
entries: If you have moved at least 20 feet before hitting a target with your Ram, you can also deal a number of d6s equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} in Cold damage to that target. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 4-6 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species
Neither bugs nor bears, bugbears are the hulking cousins of goblins and hobgoblins. They are long of limb and covered in coarse hair, with wedge-shaped ears and pointed teeth.

Despite their formidable build, bugbears - known as Tak'Garun in their homeland of Arovatan - are a serene and disciplined people, grounded in the relentless pursuit of personal and communal excellence. Central to Tak'Garun philosophy is a steadfast commitment to tranquility and unwavering focus.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Fey Ancestry
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Opportunistic Hunter
entries: Once per turn when you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on an attack roll, you deal an additional {@damage 1d6} damage on hit.

entries.name: Long-Limbed
entries: When you make a melee attack roll on your turn, your Reach is increased by 5 feet.

entries.name: Hidden Harrier
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Stealth|XPHB} skill.

entries.name: Springborn
entries: When you reach character level 3, you always have the {@spell Sanctuary|XPHB} and {@spell Calm Emotions|XPHB} spells prepared. You can cast each of these once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast them in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast these spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells when cast with this trait (choose the ability when you select this species).

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 4-7 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species

race.name: Yuan-ti

entries: Alongside the lizardfolk and medusa, the yuan-ti of Altoras have dominated the jungles of Muhana and Jagara for untold centuries. In ancient times, they were once human, and were blessed by the great leviathan the Storm Serpent to survive the harsh jungles. This blessing transformed them, creating the yuan-ti.

Yuan-ti appear mostly human but with notable serpentine features such as slitted eyes, scaly skin, and forked tongues. Scale colors are usually simple greens and browns, but more elaborate swirls, stripes, or diamond patterns are possible, even in blues and reds.

Yuan-ti society is structured into a strict religious caste system -- The more snake features you have, the closer you are to the image of the Storm Serpent, the more responsibility to have to the temples, and thus the more respect you are owed. These leaders of the people undergo sacred rituals to morph their bodies even further, transforming themselves into malisons with higher power, or abominations ever higher.
As a yuan-ti, you have these special traits.

entries.name: Blessing of the Serpent
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Lightning and Poison damage. You also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition on yourself.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Lightning Jolt
entries: As a Magic action, you can fire a jolt of lightning. Make a ranged spell attack at a target you can see within 60 feet of you. Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this attack (you choose when you select this species). On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d8} + the ability score modifer used in the attack in Lightning damage. If the target is a creature and you score a critical hit or exceed the target's AC by 5 or more, the creature can't take {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} until the start of its next turn.
This damage increases by {@dice 1d8} at character levels 5 ({@dice 2d8}), 11 ({@dice 3d8}), and 17 ({@dice 4d8}).

entries.name: Weather the Storm
entries: When you fail an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw, you can immediately take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to succeed instead. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 4-7 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species

race.name: Koalinth

entries: As the Jagara expedition was beginning to fail, the hobgoblins knew they were destined to be pushed into the sea or perish. The arcanists of the expedition, with the help of their goblin compatriots, were able to mix the naturally adaptive goblin essence and qualities of creatures within the sea. The result is the koalinth: slender hobgoblins with bright colouration, gills, and webbed hands and feet.

Much like their ancestors, the koalinth are highly structured and militaristic. With their new adaptations and military prowess, they have since become an established nation on the coasts of Jagara, and are ready to rejoin the world stage.
As a koalinth, you have these special traits.

entries.name: Amphibious
entries: You can breathe both air and water. You also have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Aquatic Surge
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can release a burst of water from valves in your skin, teleporting yourself to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet. After this trait is used, it must be recharged. At the start of your turn, roll {@dice 1d6}. On a roll of 5+, this trait is recharged.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Fey Ancestry
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition

entries.name: Mutation
entries: Each koalinth has taken on a mutation to help them adapt to their watery environment. Choose one of the following mutations, and you gain its benefits:

items.name: Camouflage
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can blend into your environment and gain the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition. This trait lasts until you move, make an attack roll, deal damage, or cast a spell.

items.name: Chitinous Carapace
entries: Your carapace provides you a base AC of 16 (your Dexterity modifier doesn't affect this number). You can't wear light, medium, or heavy armor, but if you are using a shield, you can apply the shield's bonus as normal.

items.name: Stinging Tendrils
entries: You have tendrils which are simple melee weapons that you are proficient with and can be used to make Unarmed Strikes. They have {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} and deal {@damage 1d6} Bludgeoning damage on a hit. Once per turn when you hit a creature with your tendrils, you can force it to make a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Constitution modifier) or be {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} until the end of its next turn.

items.name: Mutation (Camouflage)
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can blend into your environment and gain the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition. This trait lasts until you move, make an attack roll, deal damage, or cast a spell.

items.name: Mutation (Chitinous Carapace)
entries: Your carapace provides you a base AC of 16 (your Dexterity modifier doesn't affect this number). You can't wear light, medium, or heavy armor, but if you are using a shield, you can apply the shield's bonus as normal.

items.name: Mutation (Stinging Tendrils)
entries: You have tendrils which are simple melee weapons that you are proficient with and can be used to make Unarmed Strikes. They have {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} and deal {@damage 1d6} Bludgeoning damage on a hit. Once per turn when you hit a creature with your tendrils, you can force it to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 10 + {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or be {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} until the end of its next turn.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 4-7 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species

race.name: Ogura

entries: Deep in the jungles of Jagara, a tribe of humans made an ancient pact with a tribe of ogres. Over time, the two groups would merge into the ogura. Sometimes called half-ogres, the ogura are towering humanoids with intense appetites and a thick build to match. The union between human and ogre has granted the ogura unique magic that allows them to draw strength from the things that they consume. Using this power, they have carved out a nation for themselves in the dense and unyielding jungles.

Their most prominent threat is the yuan-ti, who claim dominion over all of Jagara. In competition to their dinosaur mounts, the ogura have made a culture of taming and utilizing forest drakes to ride in thunderous formations.
As an ogura, you have these special traits.

entries.name: Enlightened Consumption
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can consume the flesh of a dead creature to gain power and insight. You can ask the DM {@dice 1d4} questions about something the creature has experienced in life, as the memories of those experiences are conferred to you through its flesh. Additionally, you gain one {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and proficiency in one skill that the creature had in life (you choose from the available stat block). If none are available, you gain one that is deemed appropriate by the DM. These bonuses last until you use this trait again.

entries.name: Ogre Toughness
entries: Your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum increases by 1, and it increases by 1 again whenever you gain a level.

entries.name: Powerful Build
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on any saving throw you make to avoid the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition. You also count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 6-8 feet tall)

race.name: Lamia

entries: Lamia are centaur-like creatures, their lower body resembling a lion and their upper body that of a humanoid. Though their origins are not well understood, it is said an ambitious ruler made a pact with a great demon for everlasting majesty. They were given a beautiful visage, enchanting magic, and jackalwere servants, but were simultaneously transformed into the monstrous lamia.

In the Planes of Ruin, modern lamia live in tight-knit prides or packs alongside jackalwere. They often dwell near ruins, seeking mysterious magic they can use to gain riches and influence. Lamias use magical illusions and enchantments to trick others into serving them, or luring them into ambushes. Lone lamia can be exiled from the pride or striking out as adventurers in search of their own riches and influence.
As a lamia, you have these special traits.

entries.name: Corrupting Touch
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with a corrupting touch, forcing one creature within 5 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 10 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 1d8} Psychic damage. If it fails by 5 or more, it is also {@condition Charmed|XPHB} until the end of your next turn.
This damage increases by {@dice 1d8} when you reach character levels 5 ({@dice 2d8}), 11 ({@dice 3d8}), and 17 ({@dice 4d8}).

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Innate Spells
entries: You know the *Minor Illusion* cantrip. You also know the *Disguise Self* spell, and you always have this spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this trait's spells (choose when you select this species).

entries.name: Leap
entries: With a 10-foot running start, you can {@variantrule Long Jump|XPHB} up to 30 feet.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 5-8 feet tall)

race.name: Marilin

entries: Marilin often get confused for members of yuan-ti enclaves, but their origins lie in the depths of the abyss. While many of the humans who would move to Jagara would turn to the Storm Serpent, the people who would eventually become the marilin chose to call upon a great marilith, and it bestowed them with the gifts that made it such a feared warrior. The humans grew an extra pair of arms and a large constricting snake as a tail.

Thanks to this patronage, the marilin have become a nation of adept hunters and warriors. During sacred rituals, they offer up great beasts to the marilith. Though they remain mostly solitary, the marilin are often in conflict with the yuan-ti for hunting their dinosaurs.
As a marilin, you have these special traits.

entries.name: Abyssal Resilience
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire and Poison damage. You also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition on yourself.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Extra Arms
entries: You have an extra set of arms. These arms can be used to take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action, hold shields, weapons, foci, or material components, or make somatic components to cast spells.

entries.name: Serpentine Body
entries: You have a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. Additionally, you can use your snake body to Grapple targets. While a target is {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by your body, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on each of your turns to constrict the target, dealing {@damage 2d6} Bludgeoning damage.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 5-8 feet tall)

race.name: Medusa

entries: When the magic that once transformed the yuan-ti mutated, the medusa were born. Unlike their yuan-ti cousins, however, medusae see their powers as a curse.

Though many still live in yuan-ti enclaves, the divide between the two peoples has grown steadily over time. Medusae don't fit in the traditional caste system, and their clear disdain for their "gifts" further expands the rift.

It's not uncommon for medusae to pursue solitary paths, spending time away to control their petrifying powers or carve their own path. Some have even founded monastic traditions deep in the jungles, using meditation and the monastic lifestyle to find inner peace and camaraderie.

Typical medusae have scaly skin of earthy colours, ranging from light browns to deep blacks. Their infamous petrifying gaze is noted in the intense red glow of their eyes and, instead of hair, their heads are covered in a mass of living venomous serpents.
As a medusa, you have these special traits.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 120 feet.

entries.name: Snake Hair
entries: Your snake hair are simple melee weapons which you are proficient with and can be used to make Unarmed Strikes. They have {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} and deal {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage plus {@damage 1d4} Poison damage on a hit.

entries.name: Petrifying Gaze
entries: As a Magic action, each creature in a 15-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC 10 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or be {@condition Restrained|XPHB}. The target remakes this save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success, or becoming {@condition Petrified|XPHB} instead of {@condition Restrained|XPHB} on a second failed save.
After this trait is used, it must be recharged. At the start of your turn, roll {@dice 1d6}. On a roll of 5+, this trait is recharged.

entries.name: Poison Ray
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can replace any attack with a poison ray. This ray is a ranged spell attack with a range of 120 feet. Your spellcasting ability for the ray is Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma (you choose when you select this species). On a hit, it deals Poison damage equal to {@dice 1d10} + the ability score modifier used for the attack.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 4-7 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species

race.name: Sahuagin

entries: In the waters between Unvollar and the Planes of Ruin reside the kingdoms of the sahuagin. These monstrous aquatic humanoids are known as 'sea devils' to the coastal communities, a reputation they've earned being some of the most fearsome raiders in the sea. Each sahuagin kingdom is ruled by a Baron -- a mutated sahuagin with four arms -- and are constantly in conflict with all manner of sea-faring folk: triton, sea elves, kor'rokka, any vessels that cross their territory, and especially other sahuagin kingdoms. Sahuagin often attack alongside sharks, which they can telepathically command.

Though a rare sight, some sahuagin have grown tired of unending competition and leave their kingdoms to put their strength elsewhere. These few can be found aiding merchant vessels in maneuvering dangerous waters, as marines and boarders on pirate ships, or as adventurers gaining a new reputation of their own.
As a sahuagin, you have these special traits.

entries.name: Amphibious
entries: You can breathe both air and water. You also have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Blood Frenzy
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against any creature that has the {@variantrule Bloodied|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Claws
entries: You have claws that count as simple melee weapons you are proficient with and can be used to make Unarmed Strikes. Your claws have {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse}, and deal {@damage 1d6} Slashing damage on a hit.

entries.name: Creature of the Depths
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Acid and Cold damage.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Shark Telepathy
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can force a shark within 120 feet of yourself to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 10 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or be {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you. While {@condition Charmed|XPHB} in this way, you have complete control over it, and can give it commands on your turn as a free action using a special telepathy. This control lasts until the shark is more than 120 feet away from you, or you become {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} or die.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 4-7 feet tall) or Small (about 3-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species

spell.name: Accompanying Note
entries: With a flourish, you make one attack with the weapon used in the spell's casting. If the attack deals damage, the target also takes {@damage 1d4} Thunder damage.

Hit or miss, you choose one ally within 30 feet of the target. That ally gains a +2 bonus on the first attack roll they make against the same target. This bonus lasts until the start of your next turn.

components.m: A weapon with which you have proficiency and that is worth 1+ CP

entriesHigherLevel.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d4} and the bonus to your ally's attack roll increases by +1 when you reach levels 5 ({@dice 2d4} and +3), 11 ({@dice 3d4} and +4), and 17 ({@dice 4d4} and +5).

spell.name: Bestow Greater Curse
entries: You touch a creature, and that creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become cursed for the duration of the spell. When you cast this spell, choose the nature of the curse at the DM’s discretion. Some examples are:
- While cursed, the target loses one Resistance or Immunity.
- While cursed, the target loses proficiency in one skill or saving throw.
- While cursed, the target has Disadvantage on all {@dice D20} Tests.
- While cursed, the target loses the ability to cast spells or use a certain action

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: If cast at Level 7 or 8, the duration extends to 24 hours. If cast at Level 9, the curse is permanent until dispelled.

spell.name: Blanche's Reactive Warding

time.condition: which you take when a creature other than yourself is hit by an attack or targeted by the Magic Missile spell

entries: You weave a ward of force to protect an ally within range. Until the start of your next turn, the target has a +3 bonus to its AC (including against the triggering attack) and takes no damage from the Magic Missile spell. This spell does not stack with the Shield spell.

spell.name: Commemorate to Stone
entries: When this spell is cast on the gemstone, it records whatever is spoken within the next 10 minutes in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} around the stone. The recording lasts until the duration of the spell has ended, the stone is destroyed, or the spell is cast again on the same stone. The recording can be played back at any point during the duration as an action, and ends early when you choose to (no action required). The play back can be done by anyone holding the stone.

spell.name: Controlled Blaze
entries: Make a ranged spell attack at a target within range. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d8} Fire damage and begins Burning.

Alternatively, if there is a Burning creature or object within range, you can cause the fire to jump to a new target. Make a ranged spell attack at a target within 30 feet of the Burning creature or object. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d8} Fire damage and begins Burning.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d8} at levels 5 ({@dice 2d8}), 11 ({@dice 3d8}), and 17 ({@dice 4d8}).

spell.name: Earthen Revitalization
entries: You touch the ground and channel magic through the earth. One creature that you can see within range expends a {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} Die, rolls it, and regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the value rolled plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The number of Hit Point Dice expended increases by 1 at levels 5 (2), 11 (3), and 17 (4).

spell.name: Heighten Resilience

time.condition: which you take when you fail a saving throw

entries: The spell sharpens your reflexes, bolsters your fortitude, and strengthens your resolve. Until the start of your next turn, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all saving throws (including against the triggering effect).

spell.name: Hex Wave
entries: You imbue your blade with necrotic power and slash forward, projecting a wave of energy in a 15-foot Cone. Each creature in that area must make a Wisdom saving throw. On failed save, the creature takes {@damage 3d6} Necrotic damage and subtracts {@dice 1d4} from attacks rolls and saving throws until the end of your next turn. On a success, the creature takes half damage and suffers no other effects.

components.m: a melee weapon with which you have proficiency

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d6} for each spell slot level above 2.

spell.name: Infernal Strike
entries: Empowered by infernal magic, you make one attack with the weapon used in the spell's casting. If the attack deals damage, the target also takes {@damage 2d8} Necrotic damage.

components.m: a weapon with which you have proficiency and that is worth 1+ CP

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for each spell slot level above 1.

spell.name: Obliterate
entries: With the wave of a hand and a simple command, you force a target creature within range to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target's soul is corrupted, giving them the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition and reducing their Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution scores to 5. On a successful save, the target suffers no ill effects, and the spell ends.

At the start of your next turn, the target must then make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the creatures soul is obliterated and it dies. This soul obliteration bypasses any other effect that would negate instant kills, and the creature cannot be revived by any means other than the Wish spell. On a successful save, the spell ends.

m.text: a talisman worth 5,000+ GP, which the spell consumes

spell.name: Psionic Harpoon
entries: You conjure a harpoon of psionic energy and hurl it at a target within range. Make a ranged spell attack at the target. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage and {@damage 1d4} Psychic damage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d4} for both damage types at levels 5 ({@dice 2d4} and {@dice 2d4}), 11 ({@dice 3d4} and {@dice 3d4}), and 17 ({@dice 4d4} and {@dice 4d4}).

spell.name: Scattershot
entries: You produce a shard of glass or gemstone and shatter it. Each creature in a 10-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} originating from you must make a Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage.

components.m: a small shard of glass or gemstone

entriesHigherLevel.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d6} at levels 5 ({@dice 2d6}), 11 ({@dice 3d6}), and 17 ({@dice 4d6}).

spell.name: Scornful Scream
entries: You channel your anger and release a scornful wail in a 30-foot Cone. Each creature in that area must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 3d6} Necrotic damage plus {@damage 3d6} Thunder damage and gain the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn. On a success, the creature takes half damage and is not {@condition Frightened|XPHB}.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The Necrotic or Thunder damage (your choice) increases by {@dice 1d6} for each spell slot level above 3.

spell.name: Snow Flurry Shot
entries: As you hit the target, the projectile detonates in a shower of fireflies and powdered snow. The target and each creature within 5 feet of the target takes an extra {@damage 1d4} Cold damage. Until the spell ends, each creature sheds {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 5-foot radius, attack rolls against it have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}, and it can't benefit from the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d4} for each spell slot level above 1.

spell.name: Squemlish's Friend Zone
entries: A 15-foot radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} of grass and flowers begins to grow on a point on the ground you can see within range. Creatures of your choice within that area when it appears regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 2d6} + your spellcasting ability modifier.

For the duration, when a creature of your choice starts its turn in the area, it regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 2d6} + your spellcasting ability modifier. If a creature has already been healed by this spell, it instead gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 2d6} + your spellcasting ability modifier. These {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} disappear when the spell ends.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The healing increases by {@dice 2d6} for each spell slot level above 3.

spell.name: Style Shift
entries: You run your hands through a willing creature’s hair and change its color, shape, form, and length, up to 1 foot longer or shorter. If you cast the spell multiple times, you can have up to three creatures styled at a time, and you can dismiss its effects as an action.

spell.name: Withering Bolt
entries: You fire a bolt of withering energy at a creature within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage and subtracts {@dice 1d4} from the next attack roll it makes before the end of your next turn.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d8} at levels 5 ({@dice 2d8}), 11 ({@dice 3d8}), and 17 ({@dice 4d8}).

spell.name: Wraith Strike
entries: Channeling the energies of death in the projectile, you make one ranged attack with the weapon used in the spell's casting. If the attack deals damage, it deals an extra {@damage 2d6} Necrotic damage and destabilizes the targets life force. Until the end of your next turn, whenever you or an ally hits the target with a weapon attack, they regain {@dice 1d4} Hit Points.

components.m: a ranged weapon with which you have proficiency and that is worth 1+ CP

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d6} and the healing increases by {@dice 1d4} for each spell slot level above 2.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The consort has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries: The consort has all the Eldritch Invocations you have, excluding any Pact Boons. If an invocation has limited uses, those uses are shared between you and the consort. The consort’s spellcasting ability is Intelligence or Wisdom (choose when you choose this subclass).
