subrace.name: Scorpion
entries: Your lower body is that of a scorpion, easily recognized by grasping pincers and a long segmented tail ending with a stinger. You have these additional traits.

entries.name: Gripping Claws
entries: Your claws are simple melee weapons which you are proficient with and can be used to make Unarmed Strikes. They have {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} and deals {@damage 1d4} Bludgeoning damage on a hit. When you hit a creature with your claws as part of the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can use both the {@variantrule Damage|XPHB} and the {@variantrule Grapple|XPHB} option from {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. You can use this benefit only once per turn.

entries.name: Poison Stinger
entries: Your stinger is a simple melee weapon which you are proficient with and can be used to make Unarmed Strikes. They have {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} and deal {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage on a hit. Once per turn, you can also deal {@damage 2d6} Poison damage when you hit a creature with your stinger.

subrace.name: Spider
entries: Your lower body is that of a spider, with an enlarged thorax and abdomen ending in spinnerets. You have these additional traits.

entries.name: Spinneret
entries: As an action, you can conjure a mass of webbing at a point within 60 feet of you. The webs fill a 20-foot {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} there for 1 hour. The webs are {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}, and the area within them is {@variantrule Lightly Obscured|XPHB}.

The first time a creature enters the webs on a turn or starts its turn there, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 10 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or have the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition while in the webs or until it takes an action to free itself.

The webs are flammable. Any 5-foot {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} of webs exposed to fire burns away in 1 round, dealing {@damage 2d4} Fire damage to any creature that starts its turn in the fire.
After this trait is used, it must be recharged. At the start of your turn, roll {@dice 1d6}. On a roll of 5+, this trait is recharged.

entries.name: Web Walker
entries: You ignore movement restrictions caused by webs, and you always know the location of any other creature in contact with the same web. While you have this knowledge, the creature cannot benefit from the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition against you.

background.name: Crown Guard
entries: You were a trained and trusted member of a protective unit assigned to the head of state of your country or one of their family. Whether you were discharged honorably or dishonorably, the demands of the job have become a part of you, empowering you to safeguard your companions in battle.

background.name: Deck Mage
entries: You've spent time as a Deck Mage, a spellcaster hired to provide utility and firepower to naval vessels. The wealthy of Altoras often have Deck Mages on retainer, using their manipulation of water and air to decrease their travel time. Deck Mages are a powerful asset to any ship, from the daunting navies of Tersis and Kamiralik to the fearsome orcish raiders of Heim Hjera.

background.name: Dwarven Glassblower
entries: You are either a dwarf or through long study of their craft have become familiar with their arts. Your reputation for crafting finery, be it glassteel made for weaponry or jewels fit for kings, precedes you. Artist or artisan, you bring forth wonders with your hands.

items.name: Equipment:

background.name: Fearsome Raider
entries: You grew up among the orcs of Heim Hjera and learned to sail and plunder with the best of them. Notorious for the speed and ferocity of their attacks, the orcs have a love for battle and glory.

items.name: Equipment:

background.name: Golden Courtier
entries: A native or a long-time dignitary of Muhana's Golden Court, you have balanced the art of courtly graces with the court’s demands for displays of military prowess from all its guests and residents.

items.name: Equipment:

background.name: Gondolier
entries: You have served as a ferryman on the clouds of Skyholm, using levitation and immovable rods to ferry non-flying creatures between the mountaintop islands.

background.name: Hedge Mage
entries: "With a sprinkle of whimsy and a touch of wildness, I dance between the realms. For in the hands of a Hedge Mage, even the tiniest bloom holds the potential to weave spells of awe. In nature’s embrace I find my power, for within the ordinary lies the extraordinary."

background.name: Mage Student
entries: Altoras has many fine magical institutions, from the University of Ty Ymenydd in Unvollar to the College of Spellcraft in Salvation. You were a student of such an institution, training in the ways of spellcraft to supplement your lifestyle or as the beginning of your journey into the arcane.

background.name: Maritime Sentinel
entries: You were once a marine on a fishery vessel, hunting dangerous marine Kaiju for food and safety. You’re no stranger to danger on the seas and you may even be a survivor of the Night of the Red Sea. As such, you have honed your ability to keep one eye open at all times.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Dagger|XPHB}, {@item Navigator's Tools|XPHB}, {@item Rope|XPHB}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, 21 GP; or (B) 50 GP

background.name: Master of the Sea
entries: You were taught to sail by the hobgoblins of Kamiralik, widely known to be the best sailors in the world. They imparted upon you the importance of discipline and the will to explore, and by doing so, to better oneself.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Block and Tackle|XPHB}, {@item Navigator's Tools|XPHB}, {@item Net|XPHB}, {@item Rope|XPHB}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, 20 GP; or (B) 50 GP

background.name: Quill Training
entries: You have been trained from a young age to infiltrate society and steal information. The Quills are an elven organization of scribes who record the world’s history. Many are also spies, who pass along important information to the elves of Telberec.

items.name: Equipment:

background.name: Raised Wild
entries: You were raised by halflings in the wilds of Altoras. Your kind shun all civilization, and are more at home in the canopy of the forest than in the confines of the city.

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) {@item Club|XPHB}, {@item Hunting Trap|XPHB}, {@item Traveler's Clothes|XPHB}, {@item Woodcarver's Tools}, 42 GP; or (B) 50 GP

background.name: Revolutionary Survivor
entries: You've fought and survived through a civil war in your home city, such as Salvation or Haven. You either remember the before time as the glory days or when change was less scary than things staying the same. Either way, you have a dream of what your city should be and have work to help rebuild it.

items.name: Equipment:

background.name: Root Sea Diplomat
entries: Though often found in the human city states around the northern fringes of the Root Sea, many nations send delegations of diplomats to avert war with their neighbors — and sometimes, instigate it.

background.name: Skull Taker Initiate
entries: The Skull Takers originated in Heim Hjera, its ranks are mostly clerics, paladins, and rangers. As time has progressed many from different walks of life have joined this order, to fight for the living. The order prepares its members to face undeath wherever they find it, which is reflected in the magic they train their members to wield.

optionalfeature.name: Acrobat's Enhancement
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can spend 1 Incantation Point to give one willing creature you can see within 15 feet of you {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) checks and Dexterity saving throws for 1 minute.

optionalfeature.name: Arcane Trap
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can spend 2 Incantation Points to place a glyph in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of you. This glyph is {@condition Invisible|XPHB} unless you allow a creature to see it.
When you place this glyph, choose which effect it has from the following list. The glyph activates when a creature steps on the glyph's space.

entries.name: Snaring
entries: When activated, the triggering creature must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the target is {@condition Restrained|XPHB} for 1 minute. On subsequent turns, the creature can use its {@variantrule Action|XPHB} to make a Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) check against your saving throw DC, ending the condition on a success.

entries.name: Explosive
entries: When activated, the triggering creature must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 2d10} + your Incantation Ability modifier in Force damage, or half as much on a successful one.

optionalfeature.name: Athlete's Enhancement
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can spend 1 Incantation Point to give one willing creature you can see within 15 feet of you {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) checks and Strength saving throws for 1 minute.

optionalfeature.name: Charlatan's Grace
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can spend 1 Incantation Point to give one willing creature you can see within 15 feet of you {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) checks and Charisma saving throws for 1 minute.

optionalfeature.name: Disruptive Riposte
entries: When a creature misses you with a melee attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and spend 1 Incantation Point to make a melee attack roll with a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} against that creature. If you hit, the target cannot take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} until the start of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Elemental Brand
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack roll and deal damage to it, you can spend 2 Incantation Points to also deal {@damage 2d4} Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage (your choice) and brand the creature for 1 minute. While branded, you always know its location, and it cannot benefit from the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition against you.
As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on each of your subsequent turns, you can deal another {@damage 2d4} damage of the same type to the branded creature so long as they are within 30 feet of you.

entries.name: Incantation Upgrade
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d4} for each additional Incantation Point you spend.

optionalfeature.name: Elemental Burst
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can spend 1 Incantation Point and choose a point you can see within 60 feet of you. Each creature in a 15-foot radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on that point must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 2d4} + your Incantation ability modifier in Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage (your choice), or half as much on a successful one.

entries.name: Incantation Upgrade
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 2d4} for each additional Incantation Point you spend.

optionalfeature.name: Elemental Ignition
entries: As an action, you can spend 1 Incantation Point and infuse one weapon you can see within 30 feet of you with elemental power. Choose one of the following damage types: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder. For 1 minute, the weapon deals an extra {@damage 1d4} damage of the chosen type when it hits.

entries.name: Incantation Upgrade
entries: You can target an additional weapon for each additional Incantation Point you spend.

optionalfeature.name: Forceful Strike
entries: When you hit with a weapon attack roll, you can immediately take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and spend 1 Incantation Point to push the target 10 feet directly away from you. This movement provokes {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} as if they were moving willingly.

optionalfeature.name: Night's Eye
entries: As an action, you can touch a willing creature and spend 2 Incantation Points to give it {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 150 feet for 8 hours.

entries.name: Incantation Upgrade
entries: You can target an additional creature for every 2 additional Incantation Points you spend.

optionalfeature.name: Sentinel's Vigil
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can spend 1 Incantation Point to give one willing creature you can see within 15 feet of you {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks and Wisdom saving throws for 1 minute.

optionalfeature.name: Sight Beyond Sight
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can spend 1 Incantation Point to grant yourself enhanced vision for 10 minutes. For the duration, you can see creatures and objects that have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition as if they were visible, and you can see into the Ethereal Plane. Creatures and objects there appear ghostly.

optionalfeature.name: Terrain Alteration
entries: As an action, you can spend 1 Incantation Point and choose a point you can see within 60 feet of you. The terrain in a 15-foot radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on that point becomes {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} for 1 minute. When an enemy creature moves into or within the area, it takes {@damage 2d4} Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage (your choice) for every 5 feet it travels.

optionalfeature.name: Blinding Tether
entries: When you make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} on your turn, you can expend 2 Focus Points to replace it with a Blinding Tether. One creature of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes Force damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die and is {@condition Blinded|XPHB} for 1 minute or until you lose {@status Concentration|XPHB} (as if {@status Concentration|XPHB|Concentrating} on a spell). At the end of each of its turns, the target can remake the save, ending the effect on a success.

optionalfeature.name: Deflecting Tether
entries: You can use your Deflect Attacks feature when an ally within 30 feet of you is hit with an attack roll to defend them. If you redirect the attack, the target creature must be within 5 feet of the ally if it was a melee attack or within 60 feet of the ally if it was a ranged attack.

optionalfeature.name: Fell Tether
entries: When you make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} on your turn, you can expend 1 Focus Point to replace it with a Fell Tether. One creature of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes Force damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die and is knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}. On a success, the target takes half damage only.

optionalfeature.name: Disarming Tether
entries: When you make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} on your turn, you can expend 1 Focus Point to replace it with a Disarming Tether. One creature of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes Force damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die and one item in its hand is dropped and immediately drawn to one of your free hands. If both your hands are occupied, the item drops harmlessly to your feet. On a success, the target takes half damage only.

optionalfeature.name: Hindering Tether
entries: As an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, you can expend 2 Focus Points to anchor a group of obstructive tethers to the ground at a point you can see within 60 feet of you. The tethers fill a 20-foot cube from that point for the duration. The tethers are {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}, and last for 10 minutes, or until you lose {@status Concentration|XPHB} (as if {@status Concentration|XPHB|Concentrating} on a spell).

Each creature that starts its turn in the tethers or that enters them during its turn must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is {@condition Restrained|XPHB} as long as it remains in the tethers or until it breaks free.
A creature {@condition restrained} by the tether can use its action to make a Strength saving throw. On a success, it is no longer {@condition Restrained|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Pushing Tether
entries: When you make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} on your turn, you can expend 1 Focus Point to replace it with a Pushing Tether. One creature of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes Force damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die and, if it is Large or smaller, is pushed 10 feet directly away from you. On a success, the target takes half damage only.

optionalfeature.name: Pulling Tether
entries: When you make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} on your turn, you can expend 1 Focus Point to replace it with a Pulling Tether. One creature of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes Force damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die and, if it is Large or smaller, is pulled 10 feet directly towards you. On a success, the target takes half damage only.

optionalfeature.name: Tether Momentum
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend 3 Focus Points to give yourself a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} for 1 minute, using your Tether to anchor onto your surroundings and swing around. This {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} is negated when in an environment without objects or structures to anchor onto, such as open plains or high in the sky.

optionalfeature.name: Tether Singularity
entries: As an action, you can expend 4 Focus Points to summon innumerable copies of your Tether to draw your foes in. Each enemy creature in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes Force damage equal to four rolls of your Martial Arts die and, if it is Large or smaller, is pulled to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. On a success, the creature takes half damage only.

optionalfeature.name: Tether Toss
entries: When you make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} on your turn, you can expend 1 Focus Point to replace it with a Tether Toss. Choose one object that you can see within 30 feet of you that isn't being worn or carried. The object flies in a straight line up to 90 feet in a direction you choose before falling to the ground, stopping early if it impacts against a solid surface. If the object would strike a creature, that creature must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the object strikes the target and stops moving. When the object strikes something, the object and what it strikes each take Bludgeoning damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die. On a success, the struck creature takes half damage only.

optionalfeature.name: Zip Tether
entries: When you make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} on your turn, you can expend 1 Focus Point to replace it with a Zip Tether. Choose a creature or structure within 60 feet of you. If the target is heavier than you, you are pulled to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the target and can make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} attack. On a hit, this attack deals additional damage equal to three rolls of your Martial Arts die as you slam into it with speed.

optionalfeature.name: Attar of Honesty
entries: One creature that you can see within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target can't speak a deliberate lie for 10 minutes. The creature is aware of this effect and can avoid answering questions to which it would normally respond with a lie. Such a creature can be evasive yet must be truthful.

optionalfeature.name: Caustic Kombucha
entries: You throw this caustic perfume at  a point you can see within 60 feet of you, and mist fills a 20-foot radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on that point. Each creature inside the sphere must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they take Acid damage equal to a roll of your Sneak Attack damage dice and have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on all attack rolls until the end of their next turn. On a success, the creature takes half damage and does not suffer any other effects.

optionalfeature.name: Confounding Carnation
entries: Each creature in a 20-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a  failed save, the creature is under the effects of the {@spell Confusion|XPHB} spell until the start of your next turn. On a success, the creature must move in a random direction on their turn, but is otherwise unaffected.

optionalfeature.name: Dragonblood Miasma
entries: This heavy, sweet aura surrounds the target, creating a lust for violence. One creature that you can see within 60 feet of you must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, all creatures within 15 feet of the target have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against the target for 1 minute.

optionalfeature.name: Disenchanting Frankincense
entries: You throw this perfume at a point you can see within 30 feet of you. Each creature in a 15-foot radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on that point must make a Wisdom Saving throw. On a failed save, the target loses {@status Concentration|XPHB} on any spells or other effects. In addition, for 1 minute, whenever the creature casts a spell, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the spell fail and lose any resources spent on it.

optionalfeature.name: Hesperidic Haste
entries: Choose a willing creature you can see within 30 feet of you. For 1 minute, the creature's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is doubled, and it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) and Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) checks.

optionalfeature.name: Hoary Spice
entries: This harsh mixture of hot spices saps the youth and vitality from its victim. Each creature in a 20-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes Necrotic damage equal to a roll of your Sneak Attack damage dice and gains one level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}. On a success, the creature takes half damage and suffers no other effects.

optionalfeature.name: Magnetic Miasma
entries: One creature that you can see within 30 feet of you must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved until the end of its next turn and if it moves, it must move closer to you. On a success, the target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is only reduced by 10 feet, and it can move in any direction.

optionalfeature.name: Musk of Opacity
entries: This earthy odor renders the {@condition invisible}, visible. Choose a point you can see within 30 feet of you. Each creature in a 15-foot radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on that point must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature can't benefit from the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition for 1 minute.

optionalfeature.name: Obscuring Amber
entries: You throw this perfume at a point you can see within 60 feet of you. A 20-foot radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on that point is {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|XPHB}. It lasts for 1 minute, or until a strong wind (such as one created by *Gust of Wind*) disperses it.

optionalfeature.name: Petrifying Pine
entries: You spray a chilling spritz in a 60-foot {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} that is 5 feet wide. Each creature in that area must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes Cold damage equal to a roll of your Sneak Attack damage dice. At the end of each of its turns, it must remake this saving throw, taking the same amount in Cold damage on a failed save. If a creature fails this saving throw three times, it becomes {@condition Petrified|XPHB}.
On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and this effect ends.

optionalfeature.name: Soothing Balms
entries: Choose a willing creature you can see within 30 feet of you. Roll your Sneak Attack damage dice, and the target regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the value rolled. After being targeted by this perfume, the creature becomes immune to its effects until it finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Sleeping Saffron
entries: You throw this perfume at a point you can see within 30 feet of you. Each creature in a 15-foot radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on that point must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature becomes {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} for 10 minutes, until they take damage, or until a creature uses its {@variantrule Action|XPHB} to shake it awake.

optionalfeature.name: Smokey Ash
entries: Each creature in a 20-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes Fire damage equal to a roll of your Sneak Attack damage dice, or half as much on a successful one. Flammable objects not worn or carried are lit on fire.

optionalfeature.name: Trickster's Narcissus
entries: Choose a willing creature you can see within 30 feet of you. For 10 minutes, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all Charisma ability checks. In addition, all Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) and Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB} and {@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks made against the target have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Careful Attack
entries: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack roll, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to deal extra Force damage equal to your Charisma modifier to the target. The target also cannot make {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} against you until the start of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Distant Attack
entries: Before making a weapon attack roll, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to increase the range of the attack by 30 feet. If the attack hits, it deals extra Force damage equal to your Charisma modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Empowered Attack
entries: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack roll and deal damage to it, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to deal extra Force damage equal to your Charisma modifier and reroll the weapon's damage dice. You must use the new roll.

optionalfeature.name: Extended Attack
entries: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack roll, you can spend 2 Sorcery Points to deal extra Force damage equal to your Charisma modifier and mark the target. Before the start of your next turn, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to detonate the mark, dealing Force damage equal to two times your Charisma modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Heightened Attack
entries: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack roll, you can spend 2 Sorcery Points to deal extra Force damage equal to your Charisma modifier to that creature. Until the start of your next turn, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on all attack rolls.

optionalfeature.name: Quickened Attack
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point and make a weapon attack roll. On a hit, the target takes extra Force damage equal to your Charisma modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Seeking Attack
entries: When you miss with a weapon attack roll, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to give a bonus to the attack roll equal to your Charisma modifier, potentially turning the miss into a hit. On a hit, the target takes extra Force damage equal to your Charisma modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Subtle Attack
entries: When you make a weapon attack roll, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to give yourself {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on that attack. On a hit, the attack deals Psychic damage instead of the regular weapon's damage and deals additional Psychic damage equal to your Charisma modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Transmuted Attack
entries: When you hit with a weapon attack roll and deal damage, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point and choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder. The damage of the attack becomes the chosen damage type, and deals extra damage equal to your Charisma modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Twinned Attack
entries: When you make a weapon attack roll, you can spend 2 Sorcery Points to target an additional creature within range. You use the same attack and damage rolls for both targets, and the attack deals extra Force damage equal to your Charisma modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Arcane Fallout
entries: When a creature within 60 feet takes damage from a spell, you can expend your Focus and a reaction to cosmically magnify the repercussions of that attack. A pulse of corrupted reality originates from within the creature's space and spreads out for 5 feet in every direction. Each creature caught in the pulse must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes {@damage 1d8} psychic damage and {@damage 1d8} necrotic damage and cannot regain hit points for the next minute. On a success, a target only takes half damage.

entries.name: Focus Upgrade
entries: The necrotic damage increases by {@dice 1d8} when you reach Wizard levels 5 ({@dice 2d8}), 11 ({@dice 3d8}), and 17 ({@dice 4d8}).

optionalfeature.name: Devour Magic
entries: When you are hit by a spell attack, you can expend your Focus and a reaction to absorb some or all of the magic being thrown your way. When you do, make an ability check using your spellcasting ability (DC 10 plus that spell's level). On a successful check, you can choose an expended spell slot to recover. The spell slot can have a level equal to no more than half your proficiency bonus rounded down. You then gain temporary hit points equal to five times the level of that slot.

optionalfeature.name: Fundamental Repulsion
entries: When a creature enters a space within 10 feet of you, you can spend your Focus and a reaction to create a cosmic force that repels them from you. That creature makes a Strength saving throw. On a failure, the creature is pushed back 10 feet, takes {@damage 2d8} force damage, and cannot move to any space that is within 10 feet of you until the start of your next turn. On a success, the creature only takes half damage and is pushed back 5 feet.

entries.name: Focus Upgrade
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 2d8} when you reach Wizard levels 5 ({@dice 4d8}), 11 ({@dice 6d8}), and 17 ({@dice 8d8}).

optionalfeature.name: Impending Lunge
entries: When a creature within 30 feet starts its turn, you can expend your Focus and a reaction to curse it with misfortune. The creature makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the creature falls {@condition prone} immediately, taking {@damage 2d8} force damage from the magnitude of the impact. On a success, the target takes no damage but falls {@condition prone} at the start of their next turn.

entries.name: Focus Upgrade
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 2d8} when you reach Wizard levels 5 ({@dice 4d8}), 11 ({@dice 6d8}), and 17 ({@dice 8d8}).

optionalfeature.name: Inflict Mediocrity
entries: When a creature within 60 feet makes an ability check or saving throw, but before it makes the roll, you can expend your Focus and a reaction to limit their potential. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the target takes {@damage 2d8} necrotic damage and one of its Ability Score of your choice becomes 10 until the start of their next turn. On a success, the target takes half damage and suffers no other effects.

entries.name: Focus Upgrade
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 2d8} when you reach Wizard levels 5 ({@dice 4d8}), 11 ({@dice 6d8}), and 17 ({@dice 8d8}).

optionalfeature.name: Karmic Momentum
entries: When a creature within 120 feet makes an attack roll, you can expend your Focus and a reaction to convert some of the force a creature puts into their attack into mental anguish, regardless if they hit or miss with it. That creature makes an Intelligence saving throw. On a failure, they take {@damage 2d8} psychic damage and they have disadvantage on attack rolls they make for the next minute. On a success they take half damage but suffer no additional effects.

entries.name: Focus Upgrade
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 2d8} when you reach Wizard levels 5 ({@dice 4d8}), 11 ({@dice 6d8}), and 17 ({@dice 8d8}).

optionalfeature.name: Vital Inversion
entries: When a creature within 30 feet receives an amount of healing, you can expend your Focus and a reaction to invert that magic. When you do, make an ability check using your spellcasting ability (DC 15 minus your proficiency bonus). On a successful check, instead of healing, the creature takes necrotic damage equal to the amount they were going to heal for and you regain hit points equal to that amount.

optionalfeature.name: Weapon Warping
entries: When a creature within 30 feet makes hits with an attack with a weapon, you can expend your Focus and a reaction to try to momentarily alter the composition of the weapon the target is wielding to have the rigidity of a wet noodle. When you do, make an ability check using your spellcasting ability (DC 15 minus your proficiency bonus). On a successful check, when the target rolls damage for that attack, it deals minimum damage instead. On a failure, the attack only deals {@damage 1d4} less damage.

subclassFeature.name: The Forbidden Section
entries: Most magical academies have an area of study frowned upon or reserved for advanced learning and a restricted section containing information forbidden except where circumstances demand it. The Quills of Senec, spies and information brokers who collect information about the rest of Altoras and share... most of it with the courts of the world having a collection of all forbidden secrets. You are either an exceptionally well trusted member of Senecii society to be granted stewardship of such knowledge or more likely, a furious  intellect refusing to be denied the hidden truths of your reality.

subclassFeature.name: Focus Spellcasting
entries: You've uncovered a means of casting taboo spells that has altered the way you see spellcasting as a whole. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can choose to hold your Focus. Your Focus ends if you drop it (no action required), you expend it, you become {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, or you drop {@status Concentration|XPHB} (as if {@status Concentration|XPHB|Concentrating} on a spell).

entries.name: Focus Techniques
entries: You learn one Focus Technique of your choice from the "Focus Techniques" section later in this subclass' description, which is used by expending your Focus. After using a Focus Technique, you can't use the same one again for 1 minute.

You learn one additional technique of your choice when you reach Wizard levels 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, and 17. Each time you learn a new technique, you can also replace one technique you know with a different one,

entries.name: Saving Throws
entries: If a technique requires a saving throw, the DC is your spell save DC.

entries.name: Spell Streaming
entries: You can also expend your Focus when casting any of your Wizard spells. Doing so allows you to cast it without verbal, somatic, or material components (unless they are consumed by the spell).

subclassFeature.name: Mental Brace
entries: While you are holding your Focus, when you make an Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throw or a Constitution saving throw to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB}, you gain a bonus to the roll equal to your Intelligence modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Mind-melting Magic
entries: When you expend your Focus on a spell or a Focus Technique that deals damage, each target also takes Psychic damage equal to your Intelligence modifier and is {@condition Frightened|XPHB} until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Recalculate Ramifications
entries: Whenever you fail a saving throw or are hit by an attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to succeed on the save or cause the attack to miss instead. Afterwards, you suffer one level of {@condition exhaustion}.

subclassFeature.name: Greatwyrm Patron
entries: You've made a pact with a greatwyrm: an ancient dragon that has amassed enough power to pierce mortal bounds. Its ultimate goal may be nebulous, and varies depending on the type of dragon, but more often than not these pacts are made so that the greatwyrm can reach even greater heights. Should you be a faithful servant, you might share in its hoard and power. Maybe.

subclassFeature.name: Greatwyrm Spells
entries: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Greatwyrm Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

rows: {@spell Absorb Elements|XGE}, {@spell Alter Self|XPHB}, {@spell Chromatic Orb|XPHB}, {@spell Dragon's Breath|XPHB}
entries.caption: Greatwyrm Spells

subclassFeature.name: Essence of the Dragon
entries: You've been offered a mote of the dragon's essence as part of your service. You learn to speak, read, and write Draconic.
Choose which type of dragon you have formed a pact with from the Draconic Essence table, which informs the damage type used for later features.

subclassFeature.name: Prismatic Burst
entries: When you hit with an attack roll on your turn, you can trigger a Prismatic Burst in a 10-foot radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on the target. Each enemy creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Warlock spell save DC, taking {@damage 1d8} damage of the same type as your Draconic Essence on a failed save.
You can trigger Prismatic Burst only once per turn. The damage of this feature increases by {@dice 1d8} when you reach Warlock levels 5 ({@dice 2d8}), 11 ({@dice 3d8}), and 17 ({@dice 4d8}).

subclassFeature.name: Frightful Presence
entries: When you are targeted by an attack roll, you can immediately take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to call upon the Frightful Presence of your patron and force the attacker to make a Wisdom saving throw against your Warlock spell save DC. On a failed save, the target is {@condition Frightened|XPHB} until the start of its next turn. On a success, the target is immune to this feature for 24 hours.

subclassFeature.name: Dragonsight
entries: When you are targeted by an attack roll, you can immediately take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to call upon the Frightful Presence of your patron and force the attacker to make a Wisdom saving throw against your Warlock spell save DC. On a failed save, the target is {@condition Frightened|XPHB} until the start of its next turn. On a success, the target is immune to this feature for 24 hours.

subclassFeature.name: Prismatic Warding
entries: Entrenched in your patron's element, you gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to the damage type of your Draconic Essence.

subclassFeature.name: Aspect of the Wyrm
entries: As a Magic action, you can assume the form of your patron, tasting a fraction of their power. You assume the form of a dragon for 1 minute. {@variantrule Enemy|XPHB} creatures that see you transform must make a Wisdom saving throw against your Warlock spell save DC or be {@condition Frightened|XPHB} until the start of your next turn.
This form ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), or die. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
While transformed, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Damage Immunity
entries: You gain {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the damage type of your Draconic Essence.

entries.name: Draconic Presence
entries: You grow to Large size -- along with anything you are wearing -- and your Strength score becomes equal to your Charisma score. If there isn't enough room for you to increase your size, your size doesn't change.

entries.name: Fly Speed
entries: You gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 40 feet.

entries.name: Natural Armor
entries: Your {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} becomes 17 if it's lower than that.

entries.name: Natural Weapons
entries: You have claws, fangs, and a tail that can be used as melee weapons which you are proficient with. On a hit, your fangs and tail deal {@damage 1d10} Piercing damage, and your claws deal {@damage 1d6} Slashing damage. You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on each of your turns to make an attack with your claws.

subclassFeature.name: Melody Patron
entries: When the requiem arrived to Altoras from their destroyed world, they brought with them the mystical force that swims through their souls: The Melody. As it permeated through this new land, its form evolved into a resonance; a Hum that can be heard through all things, should you but listen.

subclassFeature.name: Melody Spells
entries: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Melody Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

rows: Accompanying Note, {@spell Dissonant Whispers|XPHB}, {@spell Knock|XPHB}, {@spell Thunderwave|XPHB}, {@spell Silence|XPHB}
entries.caption: Melody Spells

subclassFeature.name: Overture
entries: Whenever you cast a Level 1+ spell with a verbal component or score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}, you can harness the resonance in one of the following ways:

items.name: Temporary Hit Points
entries: You gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the level of the spell + your Charisma modifier.

items.name: Thunderous Resonance
entries: One creature of your choice within 60 feet that can hear you takes Thunder damage equal to two times the level of the spell.

subclassFeature.name: Stage Tuning
entries: Your heartbeat is tuned to the Melody. You gain proficiency in {@skill Performance|XPHB} and one {@item Musical Instrument|XPHB} of your choice. You can also use a {@item Musical Instrument|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Warlock spells.

subclassFeature.name: Sonata
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can begin a performance that lasts for 1 minute, emanating an aura of mystical music in a 60-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. The performance ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), become {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, or die.

For the duration, your Overture feature is activated whenever you or an ally casts a Level 1+ spell with a verbal component or scores a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} within the aura. If you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, you can instead grant them to any ally within the aura.

Once you complete your performance, you can't begin a new one until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, unless you expend a Pact Magic spell slot (no action required) to restore your use of it.

subclassFeature.name: Aria
entries: Your body and soul are one with the sounds of the universe. You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Thunder damage, and you are Immune to the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition. Additionally, you can mimic sounds you hear, including someone's voice, with near perfect accuracy. Creatures must succeed on a Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check versus your Warlock spell save DC to determine the sound is falsified.

subclassFeature.name: Grand Finale
entries: As a Magic action, you can cast the {@spell Power Word Pain|XGE} spell without expending a spell slot. When you do, you can also target a second creature within 15 feet of the original target.
You can choose to cast the {@spell Power Word Stun|XPHB} spell instead when you reach Warlock level 15, or the {@spell Power Word Kill|XPHB} spell at Warlock level 17.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Consort Patron
entries: Your patron is a being of infinite knowledge, but for one reason or another this knowledge was locked away alongside the bulk of its power. Its memory shattered, it is only able to collect its physical form by making a pact with you. This pact you have formed is an intimate one, one that promises to be with you on every step of the journey; as you grow in power, it slowly regains its own.

subclassFeature.name: Consort Spells
entries: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Consort Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

rows: {@spell Darkvision|XPHB}, {@spell Detect Evil and Good|XPHB}, {@spell Enhance Ability|XPHB}, {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB}
entries.caption: Consort Spells

subclassFeature.name: Little Bird on your Shoulder
entries: You gain the Pact of the Chain eldritch invocation, if you don't already have it. The familiar summoned by that invocation must use the Consort statblock below. Choose a creature type for the consort from the Consort Details table, which also informs the languages it speaks and its immunities.

This familiar is your patron, but at a fraction of its power. It can offer you insights and make requests of you, but its memory is hazy. The link made between you via the pact is its most concrete attachment.
While summoned, the following additional rules apply:

entries.name: Independent
entries: In combat, the consort -- your patron -- is not explicitly controlled. When you give it commands, you are instead encouraging it to take a certain course of action. It is still an ally to you and your allies, but may disobey at the DM's discretion.

entries.name: Disappearance of the Familiar
entries: The consort cannot be dismissed, it will only ever disappear to a pocket dimension. The consort only dies if you do, and is similarly revived if you are revived.

entries.name: Telepathic Connection
entries: The consort can deliver any spell you cast, not just ones with a range of touch. After all, they gave them to you. The other normal restrictions apply, and you must still maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} if the spell requires it.

subclassFeature.name: Fleeting Insight
entries: In brief flashes, the consort can muster up motes of its infinite knowledge. When you make a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, the consort can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to offer this insight to you. You can roll a {@dice d6} immediately after seeing the result on the {@dice d20} and add it to the roll.
The consort can take this reaction a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier, and regains all expended uses after you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Unstable Form
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, the consort can tap into an unstable visage of its true power, taking on a powerful new form seen in the Unstable Form table for 1 minute. This form ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), or the consort drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

While in this form, the consort's game statistics are replaced by the forms statistics, but it retains its alignment, feats, languages, and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores. It also retains its {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, skill and saving throw proficiencies, and immunities and resistances, in addition to gaining the ones in the stat block. If the stat block's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} or skill or saving throw modifier is higher than the consorts, use the one in the stat block. Additionally, you can command the consort as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on your turn.

After the consort enters this form, it can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, unless you expend a Pact Magic spell slot (no action required) to restore its use of it.

subclassFeature.name: Ancient Knowledge
entries: Your bond with your patron has allowed a fraction of its true power to return. The consort's Intelligence or Wisdom score increases to 20.

In addition, it gains proficiency and {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in one skill of your choice from {@skill Arcana|XPHB}, {@skill History|XPHB}, {@skill Medicine|XPHB}, {@skill Nature|XPHB}, {@skill Survival|XPHB}, or {@skill Religion|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Unleashed Form
entries: Your patron has unlocked greater power, and is now able to transform into its Unleashed Form as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, seen in the Unleashed Form table. This form follows the same rules as its Unstable Form.

After entering its Unleashed Form, the consort can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, unless you expend a Pact Magic spell slot (no action required) to restore its use of it.

subclassFeature.name: Warblood Sorcery
entries: Your magic springs from a mystical link between the magic in your soul and the innate aptitude for weaponry. You might trace a distant ancestor to an ancient sorcerer of the past who combined the might of their sword with sorcery, or you may just be naturally gifted with the arcane and have a knack for weapons. Whatever your past, magic is inherent in your blood along with an affinity for battle. The power within your veins grants you with a natural prowess for combat, making your weapon feel like a natural extension of your body. Your place is amidst the fray, while you rely on your arcane ability to shield you from harm and your martial might to overwhelm your foes.

subclassFeature.name: Born for War
entries: You gain proficiency in light armor, medium armor, shields, and one martial weapon of your choice.
In addition, you can use a simple or martial weapon as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Sorcerer spells.

subclassFeature.name: Metamaneuvers
entries: You can tap into the wellspring of power within yourself to enhance your strikes with magical effects; you gain two Metamaneuver options from "Metamaneuver Options" later in this subclass' description.
To use an option, you must spend the number of Sorcery Points that it costs. You can only use one Metamaneuver option on an attack.
Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one of your Metamaneuver options with a different one. You gain one more option at Sorcerer levels 6, 10, 14, and 18.

subclassFeature.name: Warblood Sorcery Spells
entries: When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Sea Sorcery Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

rows: {@spell Arcane Vigor|XPHB}, {@spell Armor of Agathys|XPHB}, {@spell Misty Step|XPHB}, {@spell Shield|XPHB}
entries.caption: Warblood Sorcery Spells

subclassFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. Moreover, you can cast one of your cantrips in place of one of those attacks.

subclassFeature.name: Battle Sorcery
entries: Your martial magic now flows fiercer within you. Once on each of your turns while your Innate Sorcery is active, you can use up to two Metamaneuver options on an attack instead of one.
If more than one Metamaneuver is applied to an attack, it only deals the extra damage once.

subclassFeature.name: Paradigm of Power
entries: Your mastery of both sword and spell has reached its pinnacle. Once on each of your turns while your Innate Sorcery feature is active, you can use one Metamaneuver option without spending Sorcery Points on it, and you can use up to three Metamaneuver options on an attack instead of up to two.
Additionally, you may teleport 30 feet (no action required) once per turn before or after you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action or {@action Magic|XPHB} action.

subclassFeature.name: Sea Sorcery
entries: The Sea Sorcerer is originally a piece of UA material that was very fun and flavourful but uniquely clunky to execute, likely the reason it was never fully published. A popular homebrew, The Revised Sea Sorcerer solved the initial issues but also presented new ones. This version is a new take, combining elements from both versions and introducing new ones in the hopes to create a more cohesive experience.

subclassFeature.name: Curse of the Sea
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can curse a creature you can see within 60 feet of you for 1 minute. The curse ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), the cursed creature becomes {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, or you use this feature to curse a different target.

When you cast a spell that deals Cold damage to the cursed target or forces it to move, you can cause one of the following additional effects of your choice. You can inflict this effect only once per turn.

entries.name: Damage
entries: The cursed creature takes additional Cold damage equal to your Charisma modifier.

entries.name: Shove
entries: The cursed creature is moved 15 feet horizontally in any direction.

entries.name: Slow
entries: The cursed creature's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Sea Sorcery Spells
entries: When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Sea Sorcery Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

rows: {@spell Armor of Agathys|XPHB}, {@spell Create or Destroy Water|XPHB}, {@spell Misty Step|XPHB}, {@spell Rime's Binding Ice|FTD}
entries.caption: Sea Sorcery Spells

subclassFeature.name: Soul of the Sea
entries: Your tie to the sea grants you the ability to breathe underwater, and you have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Watery Defense
entries: You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage. In addition, you gain the ability to defend yourself by momentarily assuming a watery form. After you take damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and spend 3 Sorcery Points to gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to the damage dealt and move up to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. This movement doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

subclassFeature.name: Shifting Form
entries: Your body has taken on the properties of water, allowing you to squeeze through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide. You can also move through any creature's space without penalty.
If you end a turn in a solid object, you are shunted to the nearest unoccupied space and take {@damage 1d10} Force damage for every 5 feet you were moved.

subclassFeature.name: One with the Waves
entries: Your being is altered by the power of the sea, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Cold Immunity
entries: You are Immune to Cold damage.

entries.name: Physical Resistance
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

entries.name: Immovable
entries: You have immunity to the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} and {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition and cannot be forcefully moved against your will (excluding your Shifting Form feature).

subclassFeature.name: Riffraff
entries: While many rogues acquit themselves using stealth and guile, there are many still who use strength and intimidation. Riffraff rogues specialize in fighting dirty and looking tough. While still maintaining many of the skills a traditional rogue might, they sometimes prefer to approach life's problems with the simple solutions one can only impart with the application of a bludgeon.

subclassFeature.name: Brutalizer
entries: You gain proficiency in all simple and martial melee weapons that deal Bludgeoning damage, and those weapons can trigger your Sneak Attack. You also gain training in medium armor.
At Rogue level 5, the saving throws for your Cunning Strike feature can use your Strength instead of your Dexterity.

subclassFeature.name: Get a Hold of 'Em
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} to Grapple or Shove a creature. You can also trigger your Sneak Attack against a creature you have {@condition Grappled|XPHB} even if you don't have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the roll.

subclassFeature.name: Putting On the Squeeze
entries: You can use the mastery property of one additional weapon of your choice. After you hit a creature you have {@condition Grappled|XPHB} with a weapon's mastery property, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) and Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) checks to escape the grapple until the start of your next turn.
Additionally, at the start of each of your turns, any creature {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by you takes Bludgeoning damage equal to a roll of half your Sneak Attack damage dice (rounded down).

subclassFeature.name: Intimidating Presence
entries: With a look, your foes falter. When a creature you can see makes a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} while within 30 feet of you, you can immediately take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on that roll. The creature must be able to see you in order to be a target.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier, and regain all expended uses after you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Frightful Coercion
entries: With a word, you can bend them to your will. As an action, you can attempt to coerce a creature within 30 feet of you into doing your bidding. You issue any course of action or activity to be completed, and the target must make a Wisdom saving throw with a DC equal to 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Charisma modifier. The target must be able to hear and understand you.

On a failed save, the target pursues the coercion to the best of its ability for {@dice 1d4} days or until you or your allies deal damage to it. If the suggested activity can be completed in a shorter time, the coercion ends for the target upon completing it.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Perfumer
entries: The dwarves of Unvollar are an industrious people and many have formed clans around their craft. The most famous of these is the Perfumer clan. The perfumers have gained a reputation for their skills in not only concocting pleasant scents but also espionage and spycraft. They use these perfumes to disorient their enemies and aid their allies. A clan that has risen to power will look to higher a contingent of perfumers on retainer for the political struggles they may engage in.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiency
entries: You gain proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB}. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency in one other type of {@item artisan's tools|XPHB} of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Scent Specialist
entries: You gain access to a number of perfumes that can assist you and your allies.

entries.name: Perfumes
entries: You learn three perfumes of your choice from the "Perfume Options" section later in this subclass' description.
You learn two additional perfumes of your choice when you reach Rogue levels 9, 13, and 17. Each time you learn a new perfume, you can replace one perfume you know with a different one.

entries.name: Preparing
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can use {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} to produce the perfumes you know into empty flasks you touch. You can produce a number of these equal to two times your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, but you can't prepare more than three of the same kind.
You or a friendly creature can use these perfumes as an action, after which the perfume is consumed.

entries.name: Saving Throws
entries: If a perfume requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 + your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier (your choice) + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

subclassFeature.name: Aromatic Assault
entries: Your ability to deploy your perfumes has been trained in the crucible of combat. When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can use any perfume as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Resourceful
entries: You can put together perfumes significantly faster. When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can use {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} to prepare a number of perfumes equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, up to your usual maximum.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Combination of Notes
entries: Your exploration of perfumes has yielded you the capacity to combine scents. As an action, you can combine two of your perfumes together. On use, this consumes both perfumes and delivers both effects at once.

subclassFeature.name: Primal Warrior
entries: Rangers of this conclave are flexible and stalwart defenders of the wilds. They weave primal magic inspired by the beasts they protect in their duty, spurring mutations of horns, hooves, teeth, and claws.

subclassFeature.name: Primal Warrior Spells
entries: When you reach a Ranger level specified in the Primal Warrior Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Beast Soul Strike
entries: You can enhance your attacks with magic pulled from the primal forces of the world. Before you make an attack roll, you can choose to enhance the attack with one of the following effects. You can enhance an attack only once per turn.

subclassFeature.name: Panther's Pounce
entries: You leap up to 20 feet in any direction before making your attack roll. On a hit, you also deal {@damage 1d8} Slashing damage and the target must make a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Ram's Rush
entries: If you have moved at least 20 feet before hitting the target, you also deal {@damage 1d8} Bludgeoning damage, and you can make one melee weapon attack roll as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on this turn.

subclassFeature.name: Serpent's Sting
entries: On a hit, you also deal {@damage 1d8} Piercing damage and the target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by half, and it cannot take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} until the end of its next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Beast Cloak
entries: You imbue yourself with the magic of different beasts, granting you the following special abilities. Each of them can be used once, and you must finish a Short or Long Rest before using them again.

subclassFeature.name: Bristling Boar
entries: When you are hit by a melee attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to mantle yourself in the bristling hide of the boar. You gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to three times your Dexterity modifier, and the attacker takes Force damage equal to half the damage dealt to you by the attack.

subclassFeature.name: Hasty Horse
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is doubled until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Goading Gorilla
entries: As an action, you challenge your foes with the might of the silverback. Creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you that can see you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature must direct hostile actions towards you and it can't willingly move to a space that is more than 30 feet away from you for 1 minute. A creature affected by this can remake the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

subclassFeature.name: Falcon's Flight
entries: You can channel the spirit of a noble falcon to take flight. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} for 1 minute or until you become {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Dexterity modifier, and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Chimeric Animus
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you take on a chimeric form, infusing yourself with the power of numerous beasts for 1 minute. For the duration, you gain the following benefits. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Blindsight
entries: You gain {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Regeneration
entries: At the start of each of your turns, you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Resistance
entries: You gain a +2 bonus to your {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} and {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of the Aegis
entries: On the island of Arovatan, hobgoblin monks have been honing their craft for centuries to create the ultimate warrior: One perfect weapon of mind, body, soul, and tool. The product of this order is the Warrior of Weaponcraft, an artisan and warrior wielding a uniquely crafted weapon and offers no weaknesses.

subclassFeature.name: Divine Bulwark
entries: As a Magic action, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity and choose a number of creatures up to or equal to your Charisma modifier, which can include you. Those chosen creatures gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to two times your Paladin level.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of the Aegis Spells
entries: When you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of the Aegis Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

rows: {@spell Mass Cure Wounds|XPHB}, {@spell Wall of Stone|XPHB}
entries.caption: Oath of the Aegis Spells

subclassFeature.name: Rapid Response
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to bolster your ability to defend and aid others for 10 minutes. As part of this same {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, and as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on subsequent turns for the duration, you choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. You immediately move to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the target and use your Lay on Hands feature as part of this same {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. Opportunity attacks made against you during this movement have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Assistance
entries: When you restore {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to yourself or an ally within your Aura of Protection, they restore additional {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Charisma modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Defense of the Meek
entries: When an ally you can see is hit by an attack within 60 feet of you, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to give it a +2 bonus to its AC (including against the triggering attack) until the start of its next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Aegis Form
entries: You can become a paragon of protection. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you gain the following benefits for 1 minute. Once this feature is used, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

entries.name: Double Healing
entries: When you restore {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to yourself or an ally, the total amount of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} restored is doubled.

entries.name: Sanctuary
entries: Allies within 5 feet of you are considered to be under the effects of the {@spell Sanctuary|XPHB} spell.

subclassFeature.name: Warrior of Weaponcraft
entries: On the island of Arovatan, hobgoblin monks have been honing their craft for centuries to create the ultimate warrior: One perfect weapon of mind, body, soul, and tool. The product of this order is the Warrior of Weaponcraft, an artisan and warrior wielding a uniquely crafted weapon and offers no weaknesses.

subclassFeature.name: Weaponcraft
entries: You gain proficiency in {@item Tinker's Tools|XPHB} and one other type of {@item artisan's tools|XPHB} of your choice. Whenever you make an ability check that uses your proficiency with a tool, you can spend 1 Focus Point to gain a bonus to that check equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die.

subclassFeature.name: Form-Changing Weapon
entries: You've mastered two types of weaponry and the skill to craft a single armament that can shift its form between those two weapons. Choose two types of simple or martial weapon. You become proficient with those weapons and they count as Monk weapons for you.

Using your {@item Tinker's Tools|XPHB} for an hour during a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can combine two weapons in your possession to create a single weapon called a Form-Changing Weapon. These weapons must be the same types as the ones you chose above. A Form-Changing Weapon has two modes, each corresponding to one of the weapons used in creating this new one. Using a Form-Changing weapon grants you the following benefits:

items.name: Form-Change
entries: Before or after each attack made using your Form-Changing weapon, you can choose to change its mode (no action required). If you do, it swaps its form and function to that of the other weapon you used to create your Form-Changing Weapon.

items.name: Combat Momentum
entries: If you hit with each attack you make while taking the {@action Attack|XPHB} action during your turn, you can spend 1 focus point and use your bonus action to make an attack with your Form-Changing Weapon. If that attack hits, it deals extra damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die.
This extra damage increases by one roll of your Martial Arts die at Monk levels 6 (three) and 11 (four).

subclassFeature.name: Artisan of Combat
entries: Your experience with your Form-Changing weapon allows you to use the Weapon Mastery properties of each kind of weapon that you chose for your Form-Changing weapon.

subclassFeature.name: Aura Surge
entries: You can force your life-force to surge, augmenting your strength and skill when necessary. After failing a Strength- or Dexterity-based ability check, you can immediately take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and spend 1 Focus Point to give yourself a bonus equal to a roll of your Martial Arts die, potentially turning the failure into a success.

subclassFeature.name: Finishing Strike
entries: You've perfected a technique that guarantees deadly results. When you hit a {@variantrule Bloodied|XPHB} creature with an attack roll using your Combat Momentum and deal damage to it, you can spend 2 Focus Points to forgo the damage roll and instead use the maximum value for each die.

subclassFeature.name: Warrior of the Tether
entries: Warriors of the Tether follow a tradition that rides momentum and dances with flexible solids that they use as extensions of their physical form. Some other monasteries talk about distancing your physical self from the centers of conflict, you live it every day.

subclassFeature.name: Tether
entries: You gain access to a unique weapon known as a Tether. This weapon is similar to a gauntlet or bracer that extracts a long thread when activated. The Tether doesn't occupy one of your hands when being used.

The Tether counts as a simple ranged weapon that can be used when making Unarmed Strikes. It has a range of 30 feet, and deals Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die on a hit (choose the damage type when you take this subclass).

subclassFeature.name: Tether Techniques
entries: You learn two techniques from the "Tether Techniques" section later in this subclass' description, which are specialized uses for your Tether fueled by Focus Points. You can only use one Tether Technique per turn, unless otherwise specified.

You learn one additional Tether Technique when you reach Monk levels 6 (3), 10 (4), 14 (5), and 18 (6). Whenever you learn a new Tether Technique, you can replace one Tether Technique you know with a different one.

subclassFeature.name: Harmonic Acrobatics
entries: When something would cause you to be forcefully moved or fall {@condition Prone|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to avoid the effect entirely. You are still subject to any other effects that may be caused from the source.

subclassFeature.name: Extended Techniques
entries: The range of your Tether is increased to 60 feet, and when you target a creature for a Tether Technique, the range to do so is doubled.
In addition, you can use up to two Tether Techniques each turn.

subclassFeature.name: Peak Efficiency
entries: Your Tether and Focus is a complete extension of yourself. The first time you expend Focus Points each turn, you expend one less Focus Point (minimum of 0).

subclassFeature.name: Questing Knight
entries: Knightly traditions are an ancient and storied part of civilization and none are as romanticized as questing! The questing knight travels the lands with their loyal squire helping people in need and growing their renown, at least that's how the stories go. In reality there are many reasons a knight might travel the land of Altoras. Many unlanded and minor nobles travel the land to earn a title. Others travel the land as part of a sacred rite, compelled by their Knightly order to go out and fulfill a sacred oath. Whatever their reason, a knight and their squire always draw the interest and speculation of the people.

subclassFeature.name: Loyal Squire
entries: Your renown and prowess have attracted the attention of loyal squires who have pledged themselves to your service. Choose their stat block: Protector Squire, Divine Squire, or Crooked Squire.
The squire is friendly to you and your allies and obeys your commands. They are dismissed if you die.

entries.name: The Squire in Combat
entries: In combat, the squire acts during your turn. They can move and use their {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} on their own, but the only action they take is the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action, unless you take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on your turn to command them to take an action in their stat block or some other action. You can also sacrifice one of your attacks when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action to command the squire to make their own attack. If you are {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, the squire acts on their own and isn't limited to the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action.

entries.name: Replacing the Squire
entries: If the squire dies, you can replace them by spending 50 times your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} in gold. A new squire comes to your side after 1 hour with all their {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can choose a different squire who arrives at your side. You choose their stat block and appearance. If you already have a squire from this feature, the old one is dismissed when the new one arrives.

entries.name: Saving Throws
entries: If one of the squire's actions requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice) + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

subclassFeature.name: Tandem Tactician
entries: If your squire is within 5 feet of a creature, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on weapon attack rolls against that creature. You gain this benefit only once per turn.
In addition, whenever your squire hits with their Strike and deals damage, they can deal your choice of Force damage or their normal damage type.

subclassFeature.name: Chivalric Glory
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Persuasion|XPHB} skill. If you are already proficient in this skill, you instead gain proficiency in your choice of {@skill Intimidation|XPHB} or {@skill Performance|XPHB}.
In addition, whenever you make a Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check, you can treat a {@dice d20} roll of 7 or lower as an 8.

subclassFeature.name: Squire Training
entries: When you command your squire to take the Strike action, they can use it twice.
In addition, while your squire is within 15 feet of you, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} checks.

subclassFeature.name: Knight of the Realm
entries: Your renown is known across the realms. You can now have two active squires at once.
Whenever you command the squires to take an action, you can command one or both of them at the same time. They do not have to take the same action.
Whenever you replace or restore a squire, you can replace or restore one or both of them at the same time, at no extra cost.

subclassFeature.name: Ironwood Sentinel
entries: On the peaks of Unvollar, the Ironwood trees are the lifeblood of the Goliaths that live there. The Groves provide them resources to live, and the Ironwood is the heart of their friendship with their dwarven neighbors. It is little wonder then, that they have developed unique fighting styles to defend these trees. The Ironwood Sentinels are the warriors of nature charged with the defense of the Ironwood trees.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiency
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Perception|XPHB} skill. If you are already proficient in this skill, you instead gain proficiency in the {@skill Insight|XPHB} or {@skill Investigation|XPHB} skill.

subclassFeature.name: Natural Adversary
entries: When you end your turn within 5 feet of a creature, you can choose to mark them until the start of your next turn. Any creature marked by you has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls that don't target you.

subclassFeature.name: Unnatural Vigor
entries: Your fortitude is the stuff of legend. When you use your Second Wind feature, you also gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning and Piercing damage for 1 minute. This effect ends early if you become {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} or use your Second Wind feature again.

subclassFeature.name: Ever Vigilant
entries: You can no longer be {@status surprised|XPHB} and have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks to spot hidden threats or traps.

subclassFeature.name: Arboreal Interception
entries: The Ironwood is forever with you, as you are with it, and it springs from your body to aid you in battle. When an ally you can see within 30 feet of you takes Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to halve the damage dealt from that instance and store it in yourself.

After taking this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, the first time you hit with a weapon attack on your next turn, you release the stored energy and deal additional damage equal to the amount of damage reduced. The damage type is the same as the damage reduced.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Heart of the Briar
entries: When you use your Second Wind feature, the Ironwood within flourishes around you.
