For 1 minute, shifting branches spider out of your body in a 15-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. {@variantrule Enemy|XPHB} creatures treat this space as {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} and take {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage for every 5 feet they travel inside the area.
This feature ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), use your Second Wind feature again, or become {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Guardian of the Ironwood
entries: You have become a true guardian of the Ironwood. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Amberclad Reincarnation
entries: When you die, you become encased in amber. The amber casing has an AC of 18, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison and Psychic damage, {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Bludgeoning damage, and {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half your maximum {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

If the amber casing is not destroyed after 30 days, you are resurrected with 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}, and break out of the amber casing to continue your duty. If you are revived by other means during this time, you can freely break out of the amber casing.

entries.name: Revitalization
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can touch a creature, expend one of your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, and roll the die. The target regains a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the amount rolled plus your Constitution modifier.

entries.name: The Forest Remembers
entries: You stop aging, and are immune to any effects that would cause you to age.

subclassFeature.name: Incantor
entries: The Rock Gnomes of Unvollar have had to develop unique fighting techniques to survive their new environment. To stand against their forest counterparts on one side and the halflings on the other, they developed a system of minor magical abilities called incantations, and those who wield these incantations are known as incantors. The Rock Gnomes now export this knowledge to other nations, securing their neutrality in the geopolitics of Altoras.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiency
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Arcana|XPHB} skill. If you are already proficient in this skill, you instead gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in it.

subclassFeature.name: Incantations
entries: You are able to channel the ambient arcane energies in the environment to produce incantations, fueled by Incantation Points.

entries.name: Incantations
entries: You learn three incantations of your choice from the "Incantation Options" section later in this subclass' description. You learn two additional incantations when you reach Fighter levels 7, 10, and 15. Each time you learn a new incantation, you can also replace one incantation you know with a different one.

Your Incantation Ability is Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma, choose when you select this subclass. If an Incantation requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 + your Incantation Ability modifier + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Incantation Points
entries: You have a number of Incantation Points equal to two times your incantation ability modifier, and you regain all expended Incantation Points when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Components Required
entries: To use an Incantation, you must provide a verbal component and use a weapon as a focus.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Capacitor
entries: Channeling the arcane energies around you comes easier. When you use your Action Surge feature, you also regain half of your expended Incantation Points.

subclassFeature.name: Adept's Insight
entries: Your time spent channeling ambient arcane energies have made you very astute at their identification. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks to determine the source and nature of a magical effect.

In addition, you learn the {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} spell. You can cast this spell without expending a spell slot a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
The spellcasting ability for this spell is the same ability you chose for your Incantations.

subclassFeature.name: Spell Breaker
entries: You are able to disrupt magical effects from a heightened understanding of magic manipulation. You learn the {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB} spell. You can cast this spell without a spell slot a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
The spellcasting ability for this spell is the same ability you chose for your Incantations.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Revitalization
entries: When you use your Second Wind feature, you can spend Incantation Points to enhance the effect. For each Incantation Point you spend, you regain an additional {@dice 1d10} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Warrior
entries: As a member of the Circle of the Warrior, you are devoted to preserving the balance of the natural world of the Material Plane and beyond, same as every other druid. Much like the Totem Warriors of Slobratna, you made the choice to combine the strength of metal and combat with that of the elements themselves into its own tradition. Doing so has transformed you into a steadfast guardian and avenger of the elements, ready to join the frontlines of other warriors who seek to protect the world like you do.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Warrior Spells
entries: When you reach a Druid level specified in the Circle of the Warrior Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Trained for Battle
entries: You gain a Fighting Style Feat of your choice and proficiency with your choice of {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} or {@item Woodcarver's Tools|XPHB}.
In addition, you can use a simple or martial weapon as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Druid spells.

subclassFeature.name: Primal Warrior
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape feature to channel the elements and empower your combat prowess instead of shape-shifting. Currents of raw elemental energy surge around you for 1 minute, until you gain the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, or choose to dismiss it (no action required).
While your Primal Warrior is active, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Temporary Hit Points
entries: When you activate this ability, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to two times your Druid level.

entries.name: Elemental Warrior
entries: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack roll and deal damage to it, you also deal {@damage 1d8} Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage (you choose when you activate Primal Warrior).

subclassFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn. Moreover, you can cast one of your Druid cantrips in place of one of those attacks.

subclassFeature.name: Primal Mastery
entries: When you deal Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage to one or more creatures, you can inflict an extra effect to one of those targets from the following list. You can inflict this extra effect only once per turn.

entries.name: Frostbrand
entries: If you dealt Cold damage, the target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet, and it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next attack roll it makes.

entries.name: Flametongue
entries: If you dealt Fire damage, choose another creature within 5 feet of them. That creature takes Fire damage equal to two times your Wisdom modifier.

entries.name: Stormstrike
entries: If you dealt Lightning damage, the target must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target is knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}.

entries.name: Windfury
entries: If you dealt Thunder damage, the target is pushed 10 feet directly away from you.

subclassFeature.name: Elemental Overload
entries: While your Primal Warrior feature is active, when you roll Cold, Fire, Lightning or Thunder damage and roll the highest number possible on any of the dice, choose one of those dice, roll it again, and add its result to the damage total.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Grove
entries: The natural world is full of beautiful plant species, but unfortunately some of the most beautiful growths are also those that are the most at risk. The Druids of the Grove are connected to the will of The Shepherd and they use their connections to the wild to empower it to protect itself and others. The Grove allows druids to animate plantlife and spread their life-giving magics to nearby plants and animals. Druids of The Grove don’t tend to gather with others of their kind, as The Grove connects them all, and they will protect it until the very end.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Grove Spells
entries: When you reach a Druid level specified in the Circle of the Grove Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

rows: {@spell Create or Destroy Water|XPHB}, {@spell Locate Animals or Plants|XPHB}, {@spell Thorn Whip|XPHB}
entries.caption: Circle of the Grove Spells

subclassFeature.name: Plant Whisperer
entries: You learn to speak, read, and write Sylvan.

In addition, while you are in physical contact with a plant, you imbue it with limited sentience and animation, giving you the ability to communicate with them, and you can use any of the {@action Influence|XPHB} action's skill options with them.

subclassFeature.name: Summon Protector
entries: As an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape to summon a Plantlife Protector made of living or dead flora.

The Protector appears in an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you. The Protector is friendly to you and your companions and obeys your commands. See this creature's game statistics in the Plantlife Protector stat block below. You determine the Protector's appearance.

In combat, the Protector shares your initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. The only action it takes on its turn is the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action, unless you take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on your turn to command it to take another action. That action can be one in its stat block or some other action. If you are {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, the Protector can take any action of its choice, not just {@action Dodge|XPHB}.
The Protector manifests for 1 hour, until it is reduced to 0 hit points, until you use this feature to summon the Protector again, or until you die.

subclassFeature.name: Connected Roots
entries: When you or your Protector's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} are restored by a spell, you can choose another creature within 15 feet of you or your Protector. That creature also regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to two times your Wisdom modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Sturdy Bark
entries: Learning to harness the natural defenses of the Protector, you gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage, and you have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.
In addition, when you restore {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to a creature with a spell, that creature also gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to two times your Wisdom modifier.

subclassFeature.name: The Grove's Champion
entries: When you summon your Plantlife Protector, you can instead use the Sturdy Protector stat block, seen below.
In addition, when you summon your Protector, you can choose its size to be Large or Medium.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the False Moon
entries: Some sacred places in the natural world are best protected not by force but by deception. The Circle of the False Moon uses the illusory aspect of the moon to deceive and disorient hapless travelers and raiders alike. If their illusions are unable to dissuade interlopers, they can devastate their foes by channeling the moon's stolen radiance.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the False Moon Spells
entries: When you reach a Druid level specified in the Circle of the False Moon Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

rows: {@spell Mirror Image|XPHB}, {@spell Sacred Flame|XPHB}, {@spell Silent Image|XPHB}
entries.caption: Circle of the False Moon Spells

subclassFeature.name: Veil of the False Moon
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape to wreath yourself in a Veil of the reflected moon for 10 minutes. It ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), manifest it again, or have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

When you manifest your Veil and as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on your subsequent turns, you can summon an illusory copy of yourself in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of yourself. The copy is animated and mimics your expressions and gestures. The copy has an AC of 10, 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}, and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison and Psychic damage. If a creature takes the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the copy, it can determine that it is an illusion with a successful Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check against your spell save DC. If a creature discerns any copy for what it is, it identifies which is the real you until the end of your Veil.
While a copy persists, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Distract
entries: When both you and a copy are within 5 feet of a creature that can see the copy, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against that creature.

entries.name: Move
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can move any number of copies up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see within 120 feet of yourself.

subclassFeature.name: Searing Radiance
entries: Once per turn when you deal Radiant damage, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage roll.
In addition, you gain the following additional benefits while in your Veil of the False Moon.

entries.name: Cast Spells
entries: You can cast spells as though you were in a copy's space, but you must use your own senses.

subclassFeature.name: Blistering Moonlight
entries: Your Veil has grown ever stronger. You gain the following benefits while in your Veil of the False Moon.

entries.name: Blind
entries: When you or an ally within 60 feet of you is targeted with an attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to force the attacker to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the attacker is {@condition Blinded|XPHB} until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Borrowed Aptitude
entries: While your Veil of the False Moon is active, you can maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} on two spells at once so long as one of them is from the Illusion school of magic.

subclassFeature.name: Venom Domain
entries: Many seers, shamans, and oracles throughout history have conjured guidance, prophecy, and the divine through the bottom of a vial. In this way, poison and fate intertwine. Clerics of the Venom Domain utilize both to enhance themselves and destroy their enemies. As the harnessers of this divine affliction, they are agents of change and destiny, ones that are feared and desperately sought after in the same hushed breath.

subclassFeature.name: Venom Domain Spells
entries: When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Venom Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

rows: {@spell Augury|XPHB}, {@spell Comprehend Languages|XPHB}, {@spell See Invisibility|XPHB}, {@spell Ray of Sickness|XPHB}
entries.caption: Venom Domain Spells

subclassFeature.name: Ordained Affliction
entries: As a Magic {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, you can present your holy symbol and expend a use of your Channel Divinity to force one creature you can see within 60 feet of you to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target is {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} for 8 hours. This divinely instilled poisoning ignores {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

subclassFeature.name: Poisoner's Expertise
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Medicine|XPHB} skill and with the {@item Poisoner's Kit|XPHB}. You also learn the {@spell Poison Spray|XPHB} cantrip.

subclassFeature.name: Divination Master
entries: Through the venom, your mind is opened to all possibilities. All Cleric spells of the Divination school have the {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB} tag for you.

subclassFeature.name: Fated Delirium
entries: Your faith in your deity empowers the toxins you unleash. Whenever you deal Poison damage, you ignore {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage, and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison damage is treated as {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Precognitive Trance
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can enter a precognitive trance where the divine toxins flow freely through your blood for 1 minute. This trance ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), or become {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}. For the duration, you cannot be {@status surprised|XPHB}, your {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests} have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}, and attack rolls made against you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. When your trance ends, you become {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} until you use this feature again.

subclassFeature.name: Dedication Domain
entries: There are many ways to connect to the divine. Some do it through time honored and eclectic rituals, others, by the strength of their sword arm. Clerics of the Dedication domain do it through the exploration of their talents. To them, divinity is found in the happiness one feels from honing a craft, sharpening a skill, and exploring one's hobbies. Dedication Clerics understand that life can be difficult and full of challenges, but have faith that through the disciplined exploration of the different paths of life, they can gain the necessary resilience to weather those struggles.

subclassFeature.name: Dedication Domain Spells
entries: When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Dedication Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

rows: {@spell Bless|XPHB}, {@spell Borrowed Knowledge|SCC}, {@spell Enhance Ability|XPHB}, {@spell Gift of Alacrity|EGW}
{@spell Aura of Life|XPHB}, {@spell Freedom of Movement|XPHB}
entries.caption: Dedication Domain Spells

subclassFeature.name: Helping Hand
entries: You can use your Channel Divinity to channel your passions to help your allies. As a Magic {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, you present your holy symbol and expend a use of your Channel Divinity to empower yourself for 10 minutes. For the duration, you can take the {@action Help|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on your turns. When you do so you can target an ally within 5ft of you to give them advantage on their next attack, the target of the {@action Help|XPHB} can reroll one die made during this roll.
This effect ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), or become {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Tips and Tricks
entries: You gain proficiency in any combination of two languages, skills, or tools of your choice.
In addition, when you take the {@action Help|XPHB} action to Assist an {@variantrule Ability Check|XPHB}, that ally also gains a bonus to the roll equal to your Wisdom modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Practiced Proficiency
entries: Whenever you make an ability check with a skill or tool you are proficient with, you add a {@dice d4} to the result of the roll. You cannot benefit from this feature and the {@spell Guidance|XPHB} spell at the same time.

subclassFeature.name: Focused Dedication
entries: You are able to channel your divine power into the various things you are proficient in to an extraordinary degree. The bonus die from your Practiced {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB} feature increases from a {@dice d4} to a {@dice d10}. Additionally, when you take the {@action Help|XPHB} action to Assist an {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB} while under the effects of Helping Hand, that ally deals an additional {@damage 2d6} damage on a hit.

subclassFeature.name: Path of the Bone Carver
entries: Bones give structure to beings of flesh and blood, and it is said that their powerful feelings can seep into these foundations. The Bone Carvers of the Plains of Ruin have learned to bring the magic stored within the bones of the living out to serve them. These Bone Carvers use runes to draw magic from the bones and shape them for a specific task. They use their powerful emotions to then deploy this magic to their advantage. These warriors can be seen covered in the bones of beasts and humanoids alike.

subclassFeature.name: Scrimshaw
entries: You have a number of bones that are covered in magically etched markings called Scrimshaw Tokens equal to your Strength modifier. A Scrimshaw Token is expended when you use it, and you regain all expended Scrimshaw Tokens when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
While your Rage is active, you can expend a Scrimshaw Token to create one of the following effects.

subclassFeature.name: Skeletal Warding
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, choose one of Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison, Radiant, or Thunder. For 1 minute, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to the chosen damage type. You can only be under the effect of one of these Wards at a time, and it ends early if your Rage ends.

Starting at Barbarian level 6, when you hit a target with a melee attack roll and deal damage to it, you also deal {@damage 1d6} damage of the same type as your Skeletal Warding. At level 10, whenever a creature hits you with a melee attack roll, it takes {@damage 2d6} damage of the same type as your Skeletal Warding.

subclassFeature.name: Grasping Cage
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you cause bones to erupt from the earth at a creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The target must succeed on a Strength or Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your Strength modifier + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or be {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by the bones for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the target can remake the save, freeing itself on a success.
When you reach Barbarian level 6, the bones also inflict the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition. At level 10, the target also cannot cast a spell with somatic components.

subclassFeature.name: Digging Deeper
entries: You understand how to draw out the inner magic from your own bones. You can expend a Scrimshaw Token to gain one of the following benefits.

subclassFeature.name: Enhance Ability
entries: As an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, choose one of Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. For 1 hour, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on ability checks using the chosen ability.

subclassFeature.name: Land's Stride
entries: As an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, you gain a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} or {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} for 1 hour.

subclassFeature.name: Channeled Fury
entries: You can channel your Rage into the Scrimshaw Tokens as fuel, seeping your powerful emotions into the bones in place of magic. As an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, you can expend a use of your Rage to regain all your Scrimshaw Tokens. Additionally, while your Rage is active, you can expend a Scrimshaw Token to create one of the following effects.

subclassFeature.name: Essence Harvest
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, damage you deal with your weapon attacks harvest vital essence from your opponents. Until the end of your current turn, you regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the damage dealt by your weapon.

subclassFeature.name: Reflexive Reprisal
entries: When you take damage from an enemy, you can immediately take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and make a weapon attack against that enemy.

subclassFeature.name: It's In Your Bones
entries: You have learned how to pull the magic of the tokens without needing to channel your strong emotions. Your Rage no longer needs to be active in order to create effects using your Scrimshaw Tokens. Additionally, you can expend a Scrimshaw Token to create the following effects.

subclassFeature.name: Hollow Bones
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you gain a {@variantrule Flying|XPHB} {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and can hover for 1 minute. This effect ends early if your Rage ends. When this effect ends, you fall harmlessly to the ground at a rate of 60 feet per round.

subclassFeature.name: Seismic Stomp
entries: As an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, all enemy creatures in a 60-foot cone must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your Strength modifier + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or be knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: College of the Arcane Tailor
entries: Bardic Colleges teach bards many ways to imbue their performances with arcane power. The College of Arcane Tailors dedicates itself to making costumes that enthrall and intrigue. The Bardic Regalia they create are famous for being the centerpieces of great performances and powerful arcane catalysts.

subclassFeature.name: Bardic Regalia
entries: You craft your own Bardic Regalia. The Regalia counts as magical Light Armor and provides an AC of 13 + your Dexterity modifier. You can use the Regalia as an Arcane Focus for your Bard spells, and you can change its appearance at will, but it always has the appearance and material of cloth.

As a Magic action, you can extend a part of your Regalia to strike your enemies. Make a melee spell attack at a target you can see within 60 feet of you. On a hit, it takes {@damage 1d10} Force damage plus your Charisma modifier.
This damage increases by {@dice 1d10} when you reach Bard levels 5 ({@dice 2d10}), 11 ({@dice 3d10}), and 17 ({@dice 4d10}).

subclassFeature.name: Bewitching Raiments
entries: You always have the {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} spell prepared. As a Magic action, you can expend a use of Bardic Inspiration to cast {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} without expending a spell slot.

At Bard level 6, you also always have the {@spell Incite Greed|AI} spell prepared. As a Magic action, you can expend a use of Bardic Inspiration to cast {@spell Incite Greed|AI} without expending a spell slot.

subclassFeature.name: A Tailored Experience
entries: Your knowledge of weaving magic into the fabric of your Regalia has improved. Your Regalia can replicate a magic item from the Replicable Magic Items table below. This item does not require attunement even if it normally would.
You can only replicate one magic item at a time, and you can swap this item with another from the list after you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

rows: Bag of Holding, Cap of Water Breathing, Cloak of Elvenkind, Cloak of the Manta Ray, Goggles of Night, Mariner's Armor, Hat of Vermin, Handy Spice Pouch, Prosthetic Limb (must look like and be made of cloth).

Bracers of Archery, Boots of the Winterlands, Cloak of Protection, Gauntlets of Ogre Power, Gloves of Missile Snaring, Gloves of Swimming and Climbing, Gloves of Thievery, Hat of Disguise, Headband of Intellect, Helm of Telepathy, Slippers of Spider Climbing, Winged Boots
Boots of Speed, Boots of Levitation, Cloak of the Bat
entries.caption: Replicable Magic Items

subclassFeature.name: It's All in the Stitching
entries: You are able to use your mastery of magical tailoring to weave spells into the fabric of your Regalia. Your  Regalia now stores spells cast into it, holding them until you choose to use them. It can store up to a number of levels worth of spells equal to your Charisma Modifier at a time.

You can cast a spell into your Regalia by touching it as the spell is cast, expending the spell slot as normal. The spell has no effect, other than to be stored in the Regalia. If the Regalia can't hold the spell, the spell is expended with no effect. These spells appear as patches on your Regalia, but are {@condition invisible} to others unless detected by the *Detect Magic* spell or similar effects.
As a Magic action, you can open one of these patches to cast any spell stored in your Regalia. The spell cast from the Regalia is no longer stored in it, freeing up space.

subclassFeature.name: College of the Dragon Song
entries: Dragons are powerful both physically and magically, their very presence inspiring many great artists. It is no wonder that bards, masters of weaving art and magic together, are drawn to these striking beings. The College of the Dragon Song is not only inspired by the imagery of dragons, but combines bardic and draconic magic to imbue its students with the same awe inspiring qualities as their school's namesake.

subclassFeature.name: Dragon Fire Inspiration
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration and choose a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier. The next time those creatures deal damage with a weapon attack, that attack deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison damage (your choice when you activate this feature).
This damage increases by {@dice 1d6} when you reach Bard levels 5 ({@dice 2d6}), 10 ({@dice 3d6}), and 15 ({@dice 4d6}).

subclassFeature.name: Martial Training
entries: You gain proficiency in martial weapons and training with medium armor. In addition, you can use the mastery property of two kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Draconic Mantle
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you enshroud yourself in draconic might, assuming your Draconic Mantle for 1 minute. When you do so, each creature of your choice within 60 feet of you that can see you must make a Wisdom saving throw against your Bard spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature is {@condition Frightened|XPHB} for the duration of this feature.

This transformation ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), become {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, or die. Once you use this feature, you can use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending one use of your Bardic Inspiration (no action required).
While transformed, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Intimidating Presence
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) checks and you are immune to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Spectral Wings
entries: You have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Dragon Song
entries: Your mastery of the Dragon Song is at its pinnacle, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Breath Weapon
entries: As part of the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to activate Draconic Mantle and as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on subsequent turns while your Draconic Mantle is active, you can exhale a burst of elemental power in a 20-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} or 60-foot {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} that is 5 feet wide. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 4d10} + your Charisma modifier Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison damage (your choice each time you use this breath weapon) on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.

entries.name: Wings Unfurled
entries: Magical wings are now a permanent fixture of your body. You have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.
